cases.case_summary: A 42-year-old Asian woman presented with a sudden onset of high fever, shaking chills, and jaundice. She had been well until 5 days earlier, when the chills and fever began, and jaundice had appeared 2 days earlier.
cases.full_text:
A 42-year-old Asian woman presented with a sudden onset of high fever, shaking chills, and jaundice. She had been well until 5 days earlier, when the chills and fever began, and jaundice had appeared 2 days earlier.
Past biliary history: Cholangitis due to gallbladder stones, treated with laparoscopic cholecystectomy 3 months earlier.
Vital signs and physical examination: Alert; temperature 39.3 °C; blood pressure 122/61 mmHg; regular pulse 119 per minute; respiration rate within normal range; icteric skin and sclera; no abdominal or costovertebral angle tenderness.
Blood counts: Normocytic normochromic anemia with hemoglobin 9.0 g/dl; reticulocyte count 25.0%; white blood cell count 10,580/μl; platelet count 125,000/μl.
Serum bilirubin and liver enzymes: Total bilirubin 10.9 mg/dl, direct bilirubin 6.0 mg/dl, aspartate aminotransferase 49 IU/L, alanine aminotransferase 65 IU/L, alkaline phosphatase 441 IU/L, lactate dehydrogenase 550 IU/L, and γ-glutamyl transferase 301 IU/L.
Abdominal contrast-enhanced computed tomography: Splenomegaly and a distended left kidney, without signs of biliary tract obstruction.
Haptoglobin and Coombs tests: Haptoglobin 8 mg/dl (normal range 19–200 mg/dl); direct and indirect Coombs tests negative.
Peripheral blood smear: Normal red blood cells with spherocytosis.
Osmotic fragility test: Increased fragility.

cases.case_summary: A 72-year-old man presented with swelling and pain of the left lower extremity.
cases.full_text:
A 72-year-old man presented with swelling and pain of the left lower extremity.
Past medical history: History of retroperitoneal fibrosis
Vital signs and pain history: Vital signs normal; no chest pain or back pain
Magnetic resonance angiography: Occlusion of the left iliac vein
Enhanced computed tomography of the ascending aorta: Lesion maximum dimension approximately 5.3 cm, with circular wall thickness 15 mm; no entry tear or intimal flap
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate and serum IgG4: ESR 69 mm/h; serum IgG4 279 mg/dL (normal range 4–110 mg/dL)
T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging of the ascending aorta: Low signal in the thickened wall
F-18 FDG PET-CT: Heterogeneous FDG uptake around the left common iliac vein (SUV max 3.9), retroperitoneum (SUV max 6.2), and ascending aorta (SUV max 6.4)
Pathologic sampling: No pathological finding was obtained

cases.case_summary: A 32-year-old man presented with excessive left-eye lacrimation and mild ocular pain.
cases.full_text:
A 32-year-old man presented with excessive left-eye lacrimation and mild ocular pain.
Prior head trauma: Mild left-sided head trauma 1.5 years earlier.
Eyelid and diplopia history: Left-eyelid droop fluctuated during the daytime and improved significantly when washing the face with cold water. Ptosis had developed slowly over the past 4–5 months, with recurrent diplopia.
Ocular examination: Ptosis, limitation of upward, downward, and inward gaze, and mydriasis.
Ice pack test: After an ice pack was applied to the left eyelid for 2 minutes, ptosis improved significantly and the left eye opened nearly completely. The improvement was temporary and lasted only a few minutes.
Brain MRI: A 10 × 6× 7 mm nodular lesion on the left cavernous sinus lateral wall, in continuity with the third cranial nerve, isointense on T2-weighted images and gadolinium enhanced on T1-weighted images.
Brain and neck CT angiography: No thrombosed aneurysm of the posterior communicating artery and no thrombosis of the left cavernous sinus.
Repetitive nerve stimulation: Repetitive stimulation of the left facial nerve was not suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disease.
Acetylcholine receptor and muscle-specific kinase antibodies: Negative.

cases.case_summary: A 40-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician and says she is almost bleeding to death. She reports fatigue, easy bruising, and frequent nosebleeds.
cases.full_text:
A 40-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician and says she is almost bleeding to death. She reports fatigue, easy bruising, and frequent nosebleeds.
Medications: Only an oral contraceptive.
Complete blood count: Platelet count 12 × 10^9/L (normal 150–425 × 10^9/L).
Platelet count after prednisone: No improvement in the platelet count after prednisone 60 mg per day for one week.
Bone marrow biopsy: Hypercellular marrow (75%) with trilineage hematopoiesis, decreased megakaryocytes, and normal maturation of erythroid and myeloid elements.
Physical examination: Scattered petechiae and ecchymosis on the upper and lower extremities, without rashes, hepatosplenomegaly, or lymphadenopathy.
Repeat complete blood count and peripheral blood smear: Platelet count 25 × 10^9/L, with rare giant platelet forms and no platelet clumps. White blood cell count 13.9 × 10^9/L (normal 3.4–10.4 × 10^9/L), absolute neutrophil count 12.09 × 10^9/L (normal 1.8–7.7 × 10^9/L), and absolute lymphocyte count 1.39 × 10^9/L (normal 1.0–4.8 × 10^9/L). Other labs were normal.
Repeat bone marrow biopsy with CD61 immunohistochemistry: Normocellular marrow with absence of megakaryocytes and lack of immunohistochemical staining for CD61; the biopsy was reported as showing no evidence of myelodysplasia.
Bone marrow karyotype and fluorescence in situ hybridization: Normal female karyotype (46,XX). FISH did not show deletion 5q31, monosomy 7, deletion 7q31, trisomy 8, or deletion 20q.

cases.case_summary: A 16-year-old girl was referred to the neurology department with bilateral horizontal gaze palsy that started suddenly and developed overnight.
cases.full_text:
A 16-year-old girl was referred to the neurology department with bilateral horizontal gaze palsy that started suddenly and developed overnight.
Sensory symptom history: Paresthesias in both feet for 2 months, spreading over 2 weeks to the trunk at the umbilicus, and similar paresthesias in both hands about 1 year earlier.
Eye movement and pupil examination: Complete bilateral horizontal gaze palsy, with vertical gaze preserved except for slightly slowed saccades. Pupils midsize and reactive. No nystagmus, diplopia, or blurred vision.
Facial nerve examination: Mild bilateral peripheral facial nerve palsy.
Limb motor and reflex examination: Hyperreflexia in all four limbs without clonus, downgoing plantar reflexes, and no loss of muscle strength. No spasticity or ataxia.
Brain MRI: Multiple hyperintense subcortical and periventricular lesions on FLAIR and T2-weighted images, with bilateral pontine involvement of the paramedian pontine reticular formation anterior to the cerebral aqueduct.
Spinal cord MRI: Two hyperintense lesions on sagittal images, one at C7 and one adjacent to T4.
Gadolinium-enhanced MRI: The paramedian pontine reticular formation lesions did not enhance. The T4 thoracic cord lesion enhanced.
Aquaporin-4 and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody tests: Both negative.

cases.case_summary: A 44-year-old man presented to the emergency room with extreme fatigue after a few days of fever and rash.
cases.full_text:
A 44-year-old man presented to the emergency room with extreme fatigue after a few days of fever and rash.
Earlier SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR: COVID-19 was confirmed by RT-PCR, and he remained asymptomatic afterward.
Recent isolation history: The febrile illness with rash began two days after he completed 14-day home isolation.
Fever and rash: Mild intermittent fever with chills occurred with a simultaneous maculopapular abdominal rash of lesions 0.5–2 mm; the rash was non-blanching, non-pruritic, and non-tender and rapidly desquamated into annular plaques with satellite lesions.
Symptom review: Several episodes of vomiting and diarrhea without abdominal pain; no headache, myalgia, arthralgia, bleeding, mucosal involvement, coryza, sore throat, or cough.
Examination at presentation: Conscious and lucid, with blood pressure 84/52 mmHg, a feeble regular pulse at 137 beats/min, cool lower extremities, undetectable distal pulses, and prolonged capillary fill time. Temperature 38.2 °C, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 99–100% in room air, distant heart sounds, normal breath sounds, and no neurological deficit.
Inflammatory markers: Inflammatory markers were markedly elevated; specific analyte values are not given in the narrative.
Echocardiography: Global left ventricular hypokinesia, mitral and tricuspid valve regurgitation, dilation of all four chambers, pericardial effusion, and ejection fraction less than 30%.
Dengue testing: Dengue IgM was positive by ELISA; rapid tests for dengue IgM, IgG, and NS1 were negative.

cases.case_summary: An otherwise healthy 18-year-old woman at 31 weeks of pregnancy presented to clinic with fever and painful swelling of the wrists, hands, and feet for 6 hours.
cases.full_text:
An otherwise healthy 18-year-old woman at 31 weeks of pregnancy presented to clinic with fever and painful swelling of the wrists, hands, and feet for 6 hours.
Presenting symptoms: Fever and painful swollen wrists, hands, and feet for 6 hours; unable to make a fist; difficulty walking; headache; no nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or myalgia; pruritic erythematous rash on the abdomen.
Illness among neighbors: Several neighbors had fever and arthralgia within the past week. No family members had a similar illness.
Vital signs: Temperature 38.1 °C, blood pressure 100/40 mmHg, pulse 126 beats/min, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Admission examination: Maculopapular rashes on the cheeks, nose, forehead, and abdominal wall; cervical lymph nodes not palpable; heart and lung examinations unremarkable; arthritis of both wrists and ankles and all metatarsophalangeal joints.
Left wrist arthrocentesis: Clear yellow synovial fluid with high viscosity (0.1 CCS). Gram stain showed no organisms.
Dengue serology: Dengue NS1 antigen, IgM, and IgG were negative.
Skin examination and Tzanck smear: Vesicular rash along both thighs, legs, and abdomen, with bullae on the perineum and buttocks. Tzanck smear showed no multinucleated giant cells.
Chikungunya virus RNA PCR: Positive for CHIKV RNA, reported 1 week after admission.

cases.case_summary: An 80-year-old man presented to dermatology with a 2-year history of dusky, erythematous, indurated patches on the lower abdomen and back and a more hyperpigmented plaque on the right upper calf.
cases.full_text:
An 80-year-old man presented to dermatology with a 2-year history of dusky, erythematous, indurated patches on the lower abdomen and back and a more hyperpigmented plaque on the right upper calf.
Hematologic history: Immunoglobulin G kappa smoldering myeloma diagnosed 13 years earlier
Earlier similar eruption: Similar lesions 6 years earlier improved partially with topical corticosteroid therapy and resolved completely after 9 months of lenalidomide
Skin examination: Two-year history of dusky, erythematous, indurated patches on the lower abdomen and back and a more hyperpigmented plaque on the right upper calf
Right calf skin biopsy: Dermal sclerosis with hyalinized collagen bundles extending into the subcutis, and CD34-positive dermal dendrocytes absent in the sclerotic zones
Right back skin biopsy: Dermal sclerosis with abundant interstitial dermal mucin, and CD34-positive dermal dendrocytes diminished in the sclerotic zone
Colloidal iron stain: Increased dermal mucin between the splayed collagen bundles
Laboratory studies: Persistent immunoglobulin G monoclonal gammopathy, kappa restricted, with otherwise normal laboratory tests
Clinical examination and whole-body computed tomography: No other evidence of systemic mucinosis detected clinically or on whole-body computed tomography

cases.case_summary: A 60-year-old man presented to the hospital with fever and confusion.
cases.full_text:
A 60-year-old man presented to the hospital with fever and confusion.
Brain biopsy: Left frontal lobe biopsy diagnosed as glioblastoma (WHO grade IV)
Vital signs: Temperature 39.7 °C (103.4 °F) and pulse 88/min
Physical examination: Left facial weakness and decreased right upper and lower extremity strength; remainder unremarkable
Blood counts: WBC 0.4 K/mm3 (absolute neutrophil count 0.2 K/mm3), hemoglobin 12.3 g/dL, platelets 20 K/mm3
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis: 0 WBCs/mm3, 0 RBCs/mm3, protein 100 mg/dL, glucose 33 mg/dL, LDH 38 IU/L, Gram stain negative
Electroencephalography: Generalized background slowing with left frontotemporal low-amplitude sharp waves
Repeat brain MRI: New signal abnormality in the right temporal lobe
Cerebrospinal fluid PCR: Qualitative PCR positive for HSV-1, confirmed on repeat testing on hospital day 16

cases.case_summary: A 59-year-old man presented with interval enlargement of an endophytic right interpolar Bosniak III renal cyst on surveillance imaging.
cases.full_text:
A 59-year-old man presented with interval enlargement of an endophytic right interpolar Bosniak III renal cyst on surveillance imaging.
Family history: No family history of genitourinary malignancy or renal cancer, and no history of skin or uterine leiomyomas.
Prior renal imaging: Mild bilateral cystic disease.
Surveillance renal imaging: Interval increase in size of an endophytic right interpolar Bosniak III renal cyst.
Renal mass size: 1.9 × 2.0 × 1.6 cm renal mass.
Histologic architecture: Well-circumscribed mass of cysts ranging from small, closely packed tubules to larger simple cysts, separated by fibrous stroma, with some papillary architecture.
Tumor cell morphology: Cyst lining was predominantly a single layer and occasionally multiple layers of cells with variable eosinophilic cytoplasm resembling oncocytic cells; hobnail cells, focal intracytoplasmic vacuoles, and prominent grade 3 nucleoli were present.
Stromal histology: Ovarian-type stroma was absent.
Immunohistochemistry: Focally positive for CK7 and 34-beta-E12; diffusely positive for AMACR and vimentin; fumarate hydratase loss not detected; weakly positive for RCC; negative for S100 protein and c-kit; Ki-67 proliferative activity was low.

cases.case_summary: A 65-year-old woman presented with a two-week history of left lower extremity swelling and pain.
cases.full_text:
A 65-year-old woman presented with a two-week history of left lower extremity swelling and pain.
Symptom course and associated symptoms: Swelling slightly improved with leg elevation, and pain was partially alleviated with NSAIDs. She denied shortness of breath, recent trauma, fever, chest pain, and unexplained weight loss.
Physical examination: Pitting edema of the left lower extremity, strong peripheral pulses, and a soft, nondistended abdomen.
Left lower extremity ultrasound: Negative for deep venous thrombosis.
CT angiography of the abdomen and pelvis: Large heterogeneous left pelvic retroperitoneal mass centered at the left iliac chain, measuring 8.7 × 6.9 × 8.5 cm, with probable compression/occlusion of the adjacent iliac vein.
Immunohistochemical staining: Tumor cells diffusely and strongly positive for SOX10 and negative for CK7, CK20, GATA3, and PAX8.
S100 immunostain and BRAF mutation testing: Tumor cells positive for S100, with a BRAF V600E mutation.
Brain MRI and full-body PET scan: MRI of the brain and brainstem without contrast and a full-body PET scan were unremarkable.
Dermatologic skin examination: Detailed skin examination found no primary lesion.

cases.case_summary: A 49-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with cramping abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea that had started a few weeks earlier.
cases.full_text:
A 49-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with cramping abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea that had started a few weeks earlier.
Prior abdominal and pelvic CT: Contrast CT showed fluid-filled bowels and a thickened colonic wall. She was discharged on empirical antibiotics, and the symptoms recurred soon after discharge.
Gastrointestinal symptoms: A few weeks of cramping abdominal pain, at first generalized and then localized to the epigastrium without radiation, with vomiting and frequent watery to loose, non-bloody bowel movements.
Associated symptoms and exposures: No dysphagia, odynophagia, fever, chills, skin rash, or joint pain. No recent travel, sick contacts, or antibiotic use before the symptoms began.
Leukocyte count and differential: White blood cells 9,000 cells/µL, with 28% eosinophils and an absolute eosinophil count of 2520 eosinophils/µL.
Stool pathogen testing: PCR was negative for Shigella, E. coli, Campylobacter, Clostridioides difficile toxin A/B, Salmonella, cryptosporidium, cyclospora, and enteric viruses. Microscopy for ova and parasites was negative.
Chest radiograph: No infiltrates or hilar adenopathy.
Upper endoscopy mucosal biopsies: Eosinophil-predominant mucosal inflammatory infiltrates in all specimens from the esophagus, stomach, duodenum, and jejunum. Helicobacter pylori was negative, with no villous abnormality, cryptitis, or crypt abscesses.
Duodenal biopsy: Markedly increased eosinophils, greater than 20 per high-power field, in the lamina propria, with focal epithelial involvement.

cases.case_summary: About 72 hours after admission, a maculopapular erythematous exanthema was noted, predominantly on the trunk and the upper and lower extremities.
cases.full_text:
About 72 hours after admission, a maculopapular erythematous exanthema was noted, predominantly on the trunk and the upper and lower extremities.
Admission history: 48-year-old Caucasian man with traumatic epidural hematoma and subarachnoid bleeding, intubated after rapid neurological deterioration and transferred for neurosurgical intervention.
Symptoms and exposure before admission: Fever and nonproductive cough for 3–4 days before admission, and direct contact with a person who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2.
Admission SARS-CoV-2 PCR: Positive.
Skin examination: Maculopapular erythematous exanthema predominantly on the trunk and upper and lower extremities; mucosae, palms, and soles spared.
Course after the exanthema appeared: The exanthema progressed to a papulovesicular rash, with severe septic shock requiring volume substitution and high-dose vasoactive agents and progressive respiratory failure with rapidly rising oxygen demand.
Cutaneous vesicle swab PCR: Positive for varicella zoster virus; negative for herpes simplex virus types 1–2 and SARS-CoV-2.
Varicella zoster virus serology: VZV IgM index >2.3 (negative <1.0) and VZV IgG 61 mlU/ml (negative <150); the paired earlier result was recorded as not obtained.
Tracheal secretion testing: Polymicrobial bacterial flora with Staphylococcus aureus, Enterobacter cloacae, and Serratia marcescens; VZV PCR positive at 4700 GEq/ml.

cases.case_summary: A 24-year-old woman developed extreme difficulty breathing, a nonproductive cough, and generalized malaise 36 hours after delivery.
cases.full_text:
A 24-year-old woman developed extreme difficulty breathing, a nonproductive cough, and generalized malaise 36 hours after delivery.
Costovertebral angle examination: Marked right costovertebral tenderness
Blood count and urinalysis: White blood cell count 18,000/μL; urinalysis with 3+ blood, 3+ leukocyte esterase, and 49 white blood cells per high-power field
Vital signs and pulse oximetry: Temperature 40.5°C, heart rate 136 beats per minute, blood pressure 136/82 mmHg, respiratory rate 32 breaths per minute, arterial oxygen saturation 76% on room air
Blood and urine cultures: Both grew E. coli
Electrocardiogram: Sinus tachycardia with no ischemic changes
Troponin: Levels were not elevated
Transthoracic echocardiogram: Ejection fraction 35%; both ventricles hypokinetic with normal end-diastolic diameters; valvular function normal
Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography: Significant bilateral airway disease and no evidence of a pulmonary embolus

cases.case_summary: A neonate appears ill, with moderate respiratory distress, subcostal retractions, craniotabes, and a bell-shaped chest.
cases.full_text:
A neonate appears ill, with moderate respiratory distress, subcostal retractions, craniotabes, and a bell-shaped chest.
Gestational age and delivery: Female neonate delivered at 37 weeks' gestation by planned cesarean section
Neurologic examination: Extended posture and mildly decreased muscle tone
Musculoskeletal examination: Mild bowing of both femurs, normal muscle bulk, and no limb length discrepancy
Chest radiograph: Significant demineralization of the osseous structures and atypical rib morphology with a bell-shaped chest
Skeletal survey: Generalized osteopenia, prominence of the soft tissue in the scalp parietal region, metaphyseal lucencies, and mild bowing of the right proximal humerus suggesting healing fracture(s)
Laboratory studies at 24 hours of life: Serum calcium 14.3 mg/dL (normal range 8.4–10.6 mg/dL), ionized calcium 2.32 mmol/L (normal range 1–1.5 mmol/L), 25-hydroxyvitamin D 54.2 ng/mL (normal range 31–80 ng/mL), and parathyroid hormone 2116 pg/mL (normal range 15–65 pg/mL)
Neck ultrasound: No evidence of a parathyroid adenoma
CASR molecular testing: Homozygous CASR variant c.1744T>A (p.Cys582Ser)

cases.case_summary: A 53-year-old man was admitted with a significantly decreased level of consciousness. Overnight he had urinated on the bathroom floor, and the next morning his wife could not fully awaken him. He had reported progressive fatigue for the preceding two weeks but had otherwise been in his usual health.
cases.full_text:
A 53-year-old man was admitted with a significantly decreased level of consciousness. Overnight he had urinated on the bathroom floor, and the next morning his wife could not fully awaken him. He had reported progressive fatigue for the preceding two weeks but had otherwise been in his usual health.
Past medical history: Significant only for benign prostatic hypertrophy and hyperlipidemia; no history of alcohol abuse, diabetes mellitus, or liver disease.
Preceding systemic and abdominal symptoms: No fevers, chills, rigors, weight loss, chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain.
Admission vital signs and neurologic examination: Afebrile and anicteric with normal vital signs; only intermittently arousable to verbal stimuli; remainder of the exam nonfocal.
Admission blood tests, toxicology, chest X-ray, and brain imaging: Complete blood count, serum electrolytes, serum alcohol, cardiac enzymes, urine drug screen, chest X-ray, CT of the head, and MRI/MRA of the brain were normal.
Serum ammonia: 202 umol/L (normal range 11–35 umol/L).
Liver enzymes, bilirubin, and INR: AST 19 units/L (8–14 units/L), ALT 70 units/L (7–55 units/L), total bilirubin 1.4 mg/dL (0.1–1.0 mg/dL), and INR 1.12.
Liver biopsy: Mild-to-moderate centrilobular steatosis without evidence of fibrosis.
Urine orotic acid and uracil: Marked elevation of urine orotic acid and uracil.

cases.case_summary: In July 2009, she presented with right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and fevers as high as 102.4°F.
cases.full_text:
In July 2009, she presented with right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and fevers as high as 102.4°F.
Liver resection histopathology: Florid necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with pseudotumor formation
Bartonella immunofluorescence assay: Negative for Bartonella henselae and Bartonella quintana
Presenting symptoms: Right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and fevers up to 102.4°F
Abdominal CT: Several low-attenuation lesions involving both segments of the liver, the largest measuring 4.1 × 2.9 cm
Physical examination: Afebrile, no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly, and right upper quadrant tenderness without rebound tenderness or guarding
Percutaneous liver biopsy: Extensive granulomatous hepatitis with occasional fibrin rings and background mixed microvesicular and macrovesicular steatosis
Steiner silver stain of liver tissue: Negative for spirochetes and bacteria, including Bartonella species
16S rRNA PCR of formalin-fixed liver resection tissue: A 153 bp fragment of the B. henselae 16S rRNA gene was amplified and confirmed by Southern blot hybridization

cases.case_summary: A 2-year-old girl is referred to a tertiary endocrinology service for assessment of elevated TSH in the context of obesity.
cases.full_text:
A 2-year-old girl is referred to a tertiary endocrinology service for assessment of elevated TSH in the context of obesity.
Height and weight at 3 months: Height and weight were on the 99.9th centile.
Serum TSH and free T4: Two separate TSH measurements were elevated, with a normal free T4 on both occasions.
Weight, height, and body mass index: Weight 20 kg (>99.6th centile), height 93 cm (>99.6th centile), and BMI 23.2 (>99.6th centile for age and gender).
Clinical examination: Round facies, a flat occiput, and central obesity.
Serum calcium, phosphate, and parathyroid hormone: Normal calcium and phosphate, with persistently elevated parathyroid hormone.
Skeletal examination, radiographs, and bone age: No skeletal manifestations clinically or radiologically; bone age appropriate for chronological age.
GNAS1 mutation, array, and molecular analysis: No mutations identified; array and molecular analysis of GNAS1 was normal.
Methylation-sensitive PCR of the GNAS1A, NESPAS, and NESP55 differentially methylated regions: Significant loss of the maternal methylation pattern at all three sites.

cases.case_summary: On March 10, a 22-year-old man presented with a fever of 38.5°C, a dry cough, and a sore throat for 1 day and was hemodynamically stable.
cases.full_text:
On March 10, a 22-year-old man presented with a fever of 38.5°C, a dry cough, and a sore throat for 1 day and was hemodynamically stable.
Illness 8 weeks before presentation: Fever and mild upper respiratory symptoms, with basic laboratory investigations and chest CT that were not alarming.
Vital signs: Drowsy and oliguric, with GSC 13/15, heart rate 110 bpm, blood pressure 70/30 mmHg, respiratory rate 45 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 85% on room air, and temperature 39.5°C.
Emergency laboratory tests: D-dimer 1979/500 ng/mL, total CK 2058/170, IL-6 453 pg/mL, and CKMB 72/16, with hepatic and renal dysfunction, coagulopathy, leucocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and increased inflammatory markers.
Chest CT: Severity score 27/40, with bilateral scattered ground-glass opacities and consolidation of the peribronchial regions and right lower lobes.
SARS-CoV-2 PCR: Negative.
SARS-CoV-2 antibody test: Positive for IgG.
Blood, sputum, and urine cultures: No growth; cultures were ordered on day 3 and reported on day 6.
Procalcitonin: 0.08 ng/mL.

cases.case_summary: A previously healthy 17-year-old male developed fevers to 102 °F, drenching night sweats, cough, nasal congestion, and chest tightness.
cases.full_text:
A previously healthy 17-year-old male developed fevers to 102 °F, drenching night sweats, cough, nasal congestion, and chest tightness.
Nasal COVID-19 polymerase chain reaction: Positive at symptom onset.
Symptoms and home oxygen saturation on illness day seven: Acute worsening of shortness of breath, lightheadedness, two episodes of hemoptysis, and oxygen saturation 86%.
Chest computed tomography: Multiple bilateral cavitary lung lesions, largest in the left upper lobe and 6.5 cm in diameter.
Urinalysis: Negative for protein, white blood cells, and blood.
Infectious testing: Negative for HIV, tuberculosis, aspergillus, Histoplasma, and Cryptococcus; blood cultures negative from illness day eight through day eleven.
c-ANCA and proteinase 3 antibody: On illness day 13, c-ANCA titer > 1:640 and proteinase 3 antibody level 251.9 (normal < 1.0).
Percutaneous lung biopsy: Culture negative for infectious agents, with mixed perivascular inflammation and necrotic debris.
Sinus computed tomography: Normal.

cases.case_summary: A previously healthy 38-year-old man presents to the emergency room after five days of intermittent epigastric pain with occasional nausea and yellowing of his eyes and urine.
cases.full_text:
A previously healthy 38-year-old man presents to the emergency room after five days of intermittent epigastric pain with occasional nausea and yellowing of his eyes and urine.
Abdominal pain: Intermittent epigastric, nonradiating pain for five days, occasionally associated with nausea, without vomiting or diarrhea
Eye and urine color: Yellowing of the eyes and urine over five days
Physical examination: Well nourished with icteric sclera; temperature 38°C; blood pressure 110/55 mmHg; heart rate 85 beats per minute; respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute; oxygen saturation 95% on room air; normal cardiopulmonary examination; epigastric tenderness without guarding or rigidity; no palpable mass
Blood count and serum chemistries: Normochromic normocytic anemia with hemoglobin 12.3 gm/dl; total bilirubin 2.9 mg/dl; aspartate aminotransferase 167 U/L; alanine aminotransferase 443 U/L; alkaline phosphatase 424 U/L; serum lipase and amylase not elevated
Chest radiograph: Normal chest radiograph at admission
Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography: 4.1 × 2.6 cm mass in the pancreatic head encasing the portal vein with multiple central areas of nonenhancement; 1.5 cm narrowing of the mid common bile duct with mild dilation of the intrahepatic ducts; pancreatic duct not dilated
Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration: Heterogeneous hyperechoic pancreatic lesion; histopathology with areas of coagulation necrosis, lymphocytes, and epithelioid histiocytes
Acid-fast stain and mycobacterial culture: Evidence of acid-fast bacilli; cultures grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis

cases.case_summary: A 32-day-old girl presented with watery diarrhea and fever for 4 days.
cases.full_text:
A 32-day-old girl presented with watery diarrhea and fever for 4 days.
Stool history: 12-13 episodes of watery stools without mucus or blood over the last 24 hours
Admission appearance and vital signs: Toxic, tachypneic, and irritable; axillary temperature 38.4 °C; pulse 140 beats/minute; respiratory rate 30 beats/minute; blood pressure 90/60 mmHg
Hydration examination: Tenting skin turgor, sunken eyes, and a soft fontanelle
Venous blood gas and anion gap on hospital day 2: pH 7.26, bicarbonate 11.5 meq/L, anion gap 11 meq/L
Venous blood gas and chloride on hospital day 4: Diarrhea improving, with pH 7.21, bicarbonate 15 meq/L, and chloride 115 meq/L
Urine pH, sodium, specific gravity, and urine anion gap: Urine pH 6.5, sodium 105 mEq/L, specific gravity 1.012, urine anion gap positive
Serum potassium: 3 mEq/L
Urine glucose and other substances: Negative for glucose, acid ammine, ketone, lactate, and reducing substances

cases.case_summary: A 71-year-old man was transferred from a long-term acute care facility with a 2-day history of right wrist and hand pain and swelling.
cases.full_text:
A 71-year-old man was transferred from a long-term acute care facility with a 2-day history of right wrist and hand pain and swelling.
Prior arterial and venous access: Frequent arterial blood gas sampling from both radial arteries, multiple venous blood draws, and peripheral intravenous placements on both hands and arms; no arterial line was placed.
Home medications: Aspirin, atorvastatin, carvedilol, lisinopril, and as-needed sublingual nitroglycerin.
Transfer medications: Meropenem, famotidine, furosemide, and enoxaparin 90 mg (1 mg/kg bodyweight) every 12 hours subcutaneously.
Reported bleeding symptoms: Easy bruising and bleeding, along with fatigue, shortness of breath, and generalized weakness.
Admission examination of the right wrist and hand: Mildly tender and swollen, with bruising on the inside of the right wrist. Radial and ulnar pulses were palpable, sensation and motor strength were normal, and the fingers were cool to touch.
Right arm arterial duplex: Patent arterial vasculature of the right arm and digits.
Repeat right forearm and hand examination at 20 hours: New numbness and tingling in the right thumb, index, and middle fingers; marked distal forearm tenderness; increased swelling with a forearm hematoma; radial pulse no longer palpable; newly diminished palmar sensation of the first through third fingers; unable to move the right first three digits.

cases.case_summary: A 54-year-old man presented with right flank pain for eight months and a palpable mass in the right upper abdominal quadrant.
cases.full_text:
A 54-year-old man presented with right flank pain for eight months and a palpable mass in the right upper abdominal quadrant.
Presenting symptom: Right flank pain for eight months
Physical examination: Palpable mass in the right upper abdominal quadrant
Computerized tomographic scan: Enlarged right kidney up to 20 × 15 cm with hydronephrosis, nodular thickening of the pelvic lining, and enlargement of the hilar lymph nodes
Computerized tomographic scan for calculi: Multiple renal stones
Gross examination: Cystically dilated kidney with multiple papillary and solid pale tan nodules up to 2.5 cm in diameter involving almost the entire pelvicalyceal surface and thin residual renal parenchyma; ureter free of involvement
Histologic examination: Complex papillary structures lined by neoplastic cells with frequent hobnail appearance, clear cytoplasm, and large round nuclei containing distinct nucleoli
Immunohistochemistry for cytokeratin 7, hepatocyte nuclear factor-1 beta, PAX8, and CA-125: Positive for cytokeratin 7, hepatocyte nuclear factor-1 beta, and PAX8, with focal CA-125 expression
Immunohistochemistry for RCC marker antigen, CD10, uroplakin III, p63, and CK20: Negative for RCC marker antigen, CD10, uroplakin III, p63, and CK20
cases.final_diagnosis: Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the renal pelvis

cases.case_summary: A 69-year-old man presented with a four-day history of gross hematuria, oliguria, fever of 38.5°C, fatigue, and a decreased appetite.
cases.full_text:
A 69-year-old man presented with a four-day history of gross hematuria, oliguria, fever of 38.5°C, fatigue, and a decreased appetite.
Recent medications: Sunitinib 50 mg daily at bedtime had been started two weeks earlier. Hematuria persisted after stopping acetylsalicylic acid/dipyridamole, used for over 5 years after a previous stroke, discontinuing sunitinib, and a course of amoxicillin for a presumed urinary tract infection.
Blood urea nitrogen and serum creatinine: BUN 41 and creatinine 2.7 mg/dL, with a baseline creatinine of 1.0.
Hemoglobin, platelet count, and serum sodium: Hemoglobin 11.9 g/dl, platelets 68,000/mm3, and sodium 120 mEq/L.
Urine dipstick, urine sodium, and 24-hour urine protein: Dipstick positive for blood and protein, urine sodium less than 10 mEq/L, and 24-hour urine protein 484 mg.
Haptoglobin and peripheral blood smear: Haptoglobin was not decreased, and the peripheral smear showed no schistocytes.
Serum serologic panel: p-ANCA, c-ANCA, MPO, PR3, complement levels, ANA, anti-dsDNA, rheumatoid factor, hepatitis B and C panels, and cryoglobulins were all negative.
Renal biopsy: Extensive interstitial inflammation with frequent eosinophils and interstitial edema.
Renal biopsy microscopy, immunofluorescence, and ultrastructure: Occasional lymphocytic and eosinophilic tubulitis, minimal chronicity, no glomerulitis or vasculitis, no immune complex deposits on direct immunofluorescence or ultrastructural analysis, and no thrombotic microangiopathy.

cases.case_summary: A 53-year-old woman presented with insidious, gradually progressive weakness of all four limbs over two months, decreased sensation in both lower limbs, tingling in all four limbs, and urinary retention for four days.
cases.full_text:
A 53-year-old woman presented with insidious, gradually progressive weakness of all four limbs over two months, decreased sensation in both lower limbs, tingling in all four limbs, and urinary retention for four days.
Recent fever and neck pain: Low-grade fever for about one week two months earlier, which subsided spontaneously, followed by persistent dull aching neck pain and gradually progressive quadriparesis.
Neurological examination: Grade 3 power in both lower limbs and grade 4 power in both upper limbs, spasticity with exaggerated deep tendon reflexes in all four limbs, bilateral extensor plantar responses, and hypoesthesia of both lower limbs without a definite sensory level.
Hemoglobin, leukocyte count, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: Hemoglobin 8.1 g/dL, total leukocyte count 8,000/mm3, and ESR 42 mm in the first hour.
Chest radiograph: Expansile lesion involving the right 4th rib.
Magnetic resonance imaging of the cervical spine: Altered marrow signal with erosion of C5 to D1, intraspinal extension and elevation of the posterior longitudinal ligament compressing the thecal sac and spinal cord; intervertebral discs of normal height and signal intensity.
Magnetic resonance imaging of the dorsal and lumbar spine: Altered marrow signal and abnormal soft tissue involving D6, D7, D9, D10, L2 to L5, and the sacrum, with pedicle involvement at D10 and L5, thecal sac compression at D6 and in the sacrum, and large pre- and paravertebral soft tissue at the dorsal level and presacral space.
Breast ultrasonography: Hypoechoic heterogeneous right breast mass measuring 3.5 × 2.3 cm with echogenic foci; right axillary lymph nodes enlarged, the largest 2 × 0.8 cm; left breast normal.
Fine-needle aspiration cytology and Ziehl-Neelsen stain: Aspirates from the paravertebral collection and right breast lesion showed degenerated inflammatory cells in a necrotic background, without malignant cells or granuloma; Ziehl-Neelsen stain showed acid-fast bacilli in both lesions.

cases.case_summary: A 77-year-old woman presented to the cancer assessment unit with worsening exertional shortness of breath.
cases.full_text:
A 77-year-old woman presented to the cancer assessment unit with worsening exertional shortness of breath.
Recent staging CT and anticoagulation: One month earlier, CT showed stable malignant disease, new bilateral lower-lobe pulmonary emboli, and left common femoral vein thrombosis; she was treated with once-daily therapeutic-dose dalteparin.
Platelet count 3 weeks earlier: Normal at 468 × 10^9/L.
Pulse oximetry: 84% while receiving 2 L of oxygen per minute.
Admission platelet count: 29 × 10^9/L (reference 160–370 × 10^9/L).
Blood film and repeat platelet counts: Some platelet clumping and fibrin stranding; repeat counts confirmed a genuine thrombocytopenia.
Admission CT of the thorax, abdomen and pelvis: Progression of pulmonary emboli with new thrombus in the left and right main pulmonary arteries, no radiological features of right heart strain, and new mural hypodensities in the thoracic and upper abdominal aorta reported as extensive acute non-occlusive mural thrombi.
Anti-PF4-heparin IgG assay: Strongly positive for immunoglobulin G anti-PF4-heparin antibodies.
Heparin-induced platelet activation assay: Positive.

cases.case_summary: A 41-year-old man is referred by his optometrist for blurred disk margins. He has no visual symptoms.
cases.full_text:
A 41-year-old man is referred by his optometrist for blurred disk margins. He has no visual symptoms.
Prior groin lymph node assessment: One month earlier, swollen groin lymph nodes were reactive and of unknown cause.
Genital and dermatologic history: No previous STDs, genital lesions, penile discharge, or rash.
Visual function and eye examination: Visual acuity 20/25+ right eye and 20/20− left eye; Ishihara plates 11/11 in both eyes; trace left afferent pupillary defect; intraocular pressures 12 right eye and 18 left eye; asymmetric disc edema, greater in the left eye.
Contrast brain MRI and MR venography: No mass lesions or venous occlusion.
Lumbar puncture: Opening pressure 18 cm H2O, with normal protein and glucose and 72 white cells/mm3, predominantly lymphocytes.
Interval symptoms and repeat eye examination: Within 2 weeks he developed headaches and eye pain, especially when bending over, with worsening right-eye disc edema and an enlarged blind spot.
Orbit MRI: Increased optic nerve sheath fluid, especially posterior to the globes, and contrast enhancement of the optic nerve sheaths.
Serum syphilis and HIV testing: RPR positive at a titer of 1:128, confirmatory FTA-ABS positive, and HIV testing negative.

cases.case_summary: A 57-year-old woman presented to the rheumatology clinic with recurrent fever and painful leg ulcers for two months.
cases.full_text:
A 57-year-old woman presented to the rheumatology clinic with recurrent fever and painful leg ulcers for two months.
Left-ear hearing: Vertigo and decreased hearing in the left ear, felt to be full of air, with sensorineural deafness in that ear.
Chest radiograph and ESR: Fever and chills were followed by infiltrates in the right lung and an elevated ESR.
Gingival examination and paranasal sinus CT: Gingival hypertrophy, with subcutaneous soft tissue thickening of the right buccal area.
Lower-extremity examination: Erythematous tender nodules on both lower extremities.
Blood chemistry and urinalysis: Normal kidney and liver function, and no active sediment on urinalysis.
Liver biopsy: Cholestasis and multiple large irregular areas of necrosis palisaded by epithelioid cells, with granulomatous inflammation and plasma cells.
Skin biopsy: Surface ulceration with fibrinoid necrosis and vasculitis of superficial and deep dermal vessels, granuloma formation, neutrophilic infiltration, and debris.
Ulcer pus cultures: No bacterial, fungal, or mycobacterial growth.

cases.case_summary: An 18-month-old child is brought in with intermittent spiking fever, constipation, and abdominal distension since 1 month after birth, with gradual onset of the distension.
cases.full_text:
An 18-month-old child is brought in with intermittent spiking fever, constipation, and abdominal distension since 1 month after birth, with gradual onset of the distension.
Family history: A sister had a similar illness; the parents did not seek medical attention, and she died at 2 years of age.
Physical examination: Height and weight below the fifth percentile, jaundice, abdominal distension, and borderline enlargement of the liver and spleen.
Liver function tests and coagulation studies: Alkaline phosphatase 2117 U/L, SGOT 121 U/L, and gamma-GT 301 U/L, with raised total bilirubin and markedly deranged prothrombin time and INR.
Serum alpha-fetoprotein: Level of 14,831.
Abdominal ultrasound and post-contrast CT: Coarse altered liver texture with an irregular nodular appearance and multiple small hypoechoic avascular mass lesions, corresponding to non-enhancing lesions on post-contrast CT without a typical hepatocellular carcinoma enhancement pattern. The portal vein was patent, the spleen was enlarged, and there were no signs of portal hypertension.
Renal ultrasound and post-contrast CT: Both kidneys enlarged and echogenic, with poor enhancement and loss of corticomedullary distinction.
Chest radiograph, chest CT, and wrist radiographs: Expansion of the anterior ends of the ribs, particularly the left lower ribs, with loss of the provisional zone of calcification, widening of the growth plate, and flared, frayed metaphyses.
Urinary organic acid analysis: High level of succinylacetone.

cases.case_summary: A 13-year-old man presented with a 2-year history of multiple depressed skin lesions on his face.
cases.full_text:
A 13-year-old man presented with a 2-year history of multiple depressed skin lesions on his face.
Prior skin lesion course: The lesions began as asymptomatic erythematous patches and gradually developed depressed centres.
Prior antituberculous therapy: Antituberculous therapy was given for 6 months, and the skin lesions gradually progressed during treatment.
Facial skin examination: Multiple well-defined erythematous plaques on the face; the lesions are depressed with a cliff-drop border.
Neurological examination: Sensation was intact, and there was no palpable enlargement of the peripheral nerves.
Blood, urine, biochemistry, and antinuclear antibody tests: Blood and urine routine examination, biochemistry investigations, and antinuclear antibody test were within normal limits.
Purified protein derivative test: Negative.
Chest radiograph: Posterior-anterior chest radiograph showed bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.
Skin biopsy: Numerous compact epithelioid granulomas in the dermis, surrounded by a collar of sparse lymphocytes, with no evidence of acid-fast bacilli, fungi, or polarizable foreign material.

cases.case_summary: The patient developed cognitive decline, gait disturbance, and worsening headache.
cases.full_text:
The patient developed cognitive decline, gait disturbance, and worsening headache.
Prior symptoms and treatment: A 70-year-old man with abdominal pain and headache was prescribed nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and a mucosal protectant for 2 weeks, then referred because the symptoms were unresolved and melena had begun.
Follow-up upper endoscopy and colonoscopy: Gastric and duodenal ulcers and esophagitis had healed, but the terminal ileal ulcers and erosions had not improved after nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs were stopped.
Ileal ulcer biopsy histology: Moderate lymphocytic infiltration, with no evidence of malignancy or cytomegalovirus infection.
Neurologic examination: Cognitive decline, mini-mental state examination score 21/25, gait disturbance, and worsening headache.
Head computed tomography: High-density areas corresponding to the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli.
Serum IgG4: 393 mg/dl (normal below 121 mg/dl).
Dural biopsy IgG4 immunostaining: More than 90 IgG4-positive cells per high-power field, with an IgG4-positive to IgG-positive ratio of 83.2%.
Gastrointestinal biopsy IgG4 immunostaining: No IgG4-positive cells in the esophagus, stomach, or duodenum. The ileal lesion had more than 20 IgG4-positive cells per high-power field and an IgG4-positive to IgG-positive ratio over 50%.

cases.case_summary: A 53-year-old woman consulted for a lump in her left breast.
cases.full_text:
A 53-year-old woman consulted for a lump in her left breast.
Family history of cancer: No family history of cancer
Breast and axillary examination: Movable, painless 3 cm nodule between the upper and lower inner quadrants of the left breast, without inflammatory signs or nipple retraction; axillary areas free
Mammography: Nodular lesion with irregular contours and peripheral calcification, classified BI-RADS 4
Breast ultrasound: Hypoechoic nodule about 32 mm with irregular polylobed contours between the superior and internal-inferior quadrants
Ultrasound-guided biopsy histology: Spindle cell proliferation without hemorrhage or necrosis
Ultrasound-guided biopsy immunohistochemistry: Positive cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and smooth muscle actin; Ki-67 25%; p63 positive
Mastectomy specimen histology and axillary lymph nodes: Poorly differentiated spindle cell tumor proliferation; 0 of 15 lymph nodes involved
Mastectomy specimen immunohistochemistry: Focal cytokeratin AE1/AE3, moderate cytoplasmic CK14, nuclear p63, and Ki-67 20%; no CK5/6, CD10, AML, or BCL2 expression; no ER, PR, or HER2 expression
cases.final_diagnosis: Spindle cell carcinoma of the breast

cases.case_summary: A 34-year-old pregnant woman is found in the first trimester to have a fetal nuchal translucency of 1.8 mm, an absent ductus venosus, and a cystic mass in the thoracic cavity. She continues the pregnancy.
cases.full_text:
A 34-year-old pregnant woman is found in the first trimester to have a fetal nuchal translucency of 1.8 mm, an absent ductus venosus, and a cystic mass in the thoracic cavity. She continues the pregnancy.
First-trimester fetal ultrasound: Nuchal translucency 1.8 mm, ductus venosus absent, and a cystic mass in the thoracic cavity
Fetal ultrasound at 19 weeks' gestation: A cystic structure extended from the pharynx to the diaphragm in the right thoracic cavity, with no gastric bubble in the abdominal cavity and no ductus venosus identified
Three-dimensional fetal ultrasound at 23 weeks' gestation: The oesophagus measured 1.5 cm and its end was connected to the cystic structure
Autopsy examination of the stomach: The whole stomach lay in the right thoracic cavity and was reversed, with the lesser curvature on the left and the greater curvature on the right
Autopsy examination of the cervical spine: Vertebral dysplasia at C2–C6, fusion and disorganization of the C2–C4 vertebral bodies, and a 0.4 × 0.3 cm anterior fissure at C5–C6; spinal cord tissue was normal
Autopsy examination of the oesophagogastric junction: The cervical spine defect was closely connected to the serosa at the transition between the oesophagus and cardia, and the cardia was fixed in front of C6
Autopsy examination of the diaphragm and upper abdominal organs: A dorsal diaphragmatic defect was present; parts of the duodenum and pancreas, the left and caudate lobes of the liver, and the whole spleen lay in the right chest, and the spleen behind the stomach had a poly-spleen malformation

cases.case_summary: A 6-year-old boy was seen for lesions in the maxilla and mandible that his parents had noticed 2 months earlier.
cases.full_text:
A 6-year-old boy was seen for lesions in the maxilla and mandible that his parents had noticed 2 months earlier.
Family history: No familial history of jaw disease.
Physical examination: Firm, non-fluctuant lesions with bilateral mandibular buccal expansion from the deciduous canine to the deciduous molar; overlying mucosa intact.
Panoramic radiography: A large lesion extended from the right ascending mandibular ramus to the left, with central heterogeneous mineralization and a thin marginal radiolucent rim with a well-demarcated sclerotic border.
Radiographic dental findings: Several tooth germs were displaced, roots of multiple primary teeth were resorbed, and permanent molars were displaced, including the second molar into the ascending ramus.
Computed tomography: Thinned cortex along the inferior mandibular border with alveolar expansion beside a mixed radiopaque mass; a displaced tooth germ extended into the maxillary sinus.
Serum biochemistry: Serum calcium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase, and PTH were within normal limits.
Incisional biopsy: Mandibular and maxillary specimens showed a similar pattern of fibrous tissue rich in fibroblasts with spherical calcifications.
GNAS and HRPT2 sequencing: No genetic abnormality in the lesions.

cases.case_summary: A 28-year-old woman was referred to an eye hospital complaining of vision loss and photopsia in both eyes for 3 years.
cases.full_text:
A 28-year-old woman was referred to an eye hospital complaining of vision loss and photopsia in both eyes for 3 years.
Drug exposure history: Accidental ingestion of four boluses of veterinary niclosamide, 1250 mg each, 3 years earlier; she reported that visual problems began a few days later.
Other medication and substance use: No other medications or drugs during this period, no alcohol use, and she denied regular smoking.
Visual symptom review: She denied nyctalopia, hemeralopia, and photophobia.
Family history: No known parental consanguinity, and family history negative for vision loss and retinal disorders.
Best-corrected visual acuity, color vision, and pupils: Best-corrected visual acuity 20/50 in the right eye and 20/63 in the left eye, with normal color vision and pupillary reactions in both eyes.
Fundus examination: Pink optic discs with a cup-to-disc ratio of 0.2 and atrophy in the parafoveal retinal pigment epithelium.
Optical coherence tomography: Disruption of the parafoveal ellipsoid zone and outer retinal thinning.
Electroretinography: Decreased scotopic and photopic amplitudes with a normal waveform in both eyes.

cases.case_summary: A 43-year-old man presented in June 2015 with a soft tissue mass in his right thigh that he had first noticed in January 2015.
cases.full_text:
A 43-year-old man presented in June 2015 with a soft tissue mass in his right thigh that he had first noticed in January 2015.
Symptom onset: Right thigh soft tissue mass originally noticed in January 2015
Physical examination: Hard, elastic mass, approximate size 30 cm, without redness, inflammation, or a pulse
Radiography: Large soft tissue mass without calcification, periosteal reaction, or infiltration into the femur
Magnetic resonance imaging: Isointense signal on T1-weighted images, high-intensity signal on T2-weighted images, and gadolinium enhancement on the side edge of the partition structure
Histopathology: Lobulated tumor with a myxoid matrix and atypical spindle-shaped cells forming an eosinophilic cord-like structure
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for S-100; negative for synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and pan keratin (AE1/AE3)
Histologic review for lipoblasts and vasculature: Lipoblasts and capillary vasculature were not present
Fluorescence in situ hybridization: EWSR1 split signal in 44/50 tumor cells (88%) and NR4A3 split signal in 47/50 tumor cells (94%)

cases.case_summary: A 20-year-old woman was referred with constant pain in the right proximal thigh that had progressed for 8 years.
cases.full_text:
A 20-year-old woman was referred with constant pain in the right proximal thigh that had progressed for 8 years.
Pain pattern: Pain aggravated at night and moderately relieved by physical activity and cold baths.
Right thigh examination: No skin lesions, café au lait spots, redness, increased temperature, or swelling in the right thigh; leg length unequal but within normality.
MRI and PET-CT of the femur: Significantly increased cortical thickness of the right femoral diaphysis partially obliterating the medullary cavity, with an uneven sclerotic surface.
Radiograph of the right femoral shaft: Irregular hyperostosis of the right femoral shaft.
Bone scintigraphy: Increased tracer uptake in most of the right femoral shaft.
Biochemical bone markers: Biochemical bone markers were normal, including alkaline phosphatase.
GNAS1 and SQSTM1 mutation screening: GNAS1 activating mutation R201 was negative in peripheral blood, and SQSTM1 mutation screening was negative.
Bone biopsy: Thickened bone springs with preserved lamellar structure and slightly accentuated cement lines; no fibrosis, inflammation, increased alcian positivity, or signs of malignancy or neoplasia.

cases.case_summary: A 55-year-old man was admitted to the emergency department with acute chest tightness, burning pain radiating to both arms, sensory impairment at the nipple level, and bilateral arm paresis within minutes.
cases.full_text:
A 55-year-old man was admitted to the emergency department with acute chest tightness, burning pain radiating to both arms, sensory impairment at the nipple level, and bilateral arm paresis within minutes.
Emergency presentation: Acute chest tightness, burning pain radiating from the chest to both upper extremities, sensory impairment at the nipple level (T4), and bilateral arm paresis within several minutes.
Limb strength: Lower left extremity strength fell from 5 to 2 on Lovett’s scale within hours, then during the stay the lower right fell from 5 to 3, the lower left from 2 to 0, and both upper extremities from 5 to 3.
Cervical spinal cord MRI: Inflammatory focus in the central part of the C5/C6 spinal cord; contrast agents did not reveal activity features.
Brain and thoracic spine MRI: No lesions on later MR images of the cerebrum and thoracic spine.
Cerebrospinal fluid protein and albumin: Total protein 0.91 g/L and albumin 656.7 mg/L, both reported as elevated.
Cerebrospinal fluid oligoclonal bands and microbiology: Intradural type 4 oligoclonal band synthesis was not observed. CSF culture and PCR for pathogens were negative, and the fluid culture was negative.
Aquaporin-4 antibody: Negative.
MOG antibody: 1:10 on 13 October 2022, described as slightly elevated; repeat on 18 October 2022 was <1:10, described as unfavorable.

cases.case_summary: A 62-year-old woman presented to hospital with two weeks of worsening temporal disorientation and unsteady gait.
cases.full_text:
A 62-year-old woman presented to hospital with two weeks of worsening temporal disorientation and unsteady gait.
Rheumatoid arthritis medication history: Rheumatoid arthritis diagnosed 10 years earlier, treated with prednisolone 10 mg daily, leflunomide 20 mg daily, and methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly; adalimumab 40 mg/0.4 mL every two weeks was added 2 months earlier and the other drugs were continued
Neurologic examination: Moderate left hemiparesis, grade 3, with no spatial disorientation, sensory disturbances, or cranial nerve injuries
Complete blood count: White blood cell count 9100 µL, neutrophils 8120 µL (89%), lymphocytes 600 µL (7%)
Body temperature: Afebrile, 36.4 °C
HIV and Toxoplasma serology: HIV type 1 seronegative; detectable serum IgG antibodies to Toxoplasma gondii and negative IgM
Brain CT: Focal space-occupying hypodense lesion in the right basal ganglia with surrounding edema, effacement of the ipsilateral sulci, ventricular buckling without hydrocephalus, and mild midline shift to the left
Brain MRI: Lesion relatively heterogeneous on T2/FLAIR with marginal enhancement after gadolinium; perfusion-weighted imaging showed a significant decrease of cerebral blood flow (CBV) within the lesion
Brain biopsy: Cysts containing bradyzoites and free tachyzoites throughout the sample

cases.case_summary: A 70-year-old man was referred to urology with a new left-sided scrotal lump, noticed about 6 weeks earlier. It was not particularly painful but had increased in size.
cases.full_text:
A 70-year-old man was referred to urology with a new left-sided scrotal lump, noticed about 6 weeks earlier. It was not particularly painful but had increased in size.
Medical history: Hypertension and eczema, and a right orchidectomy with chemotherapy for testicular seminoma about 25 years earlier.
Scrotal examination: Large left hemi-scrotal swelling, with the left testis impalpable.
Baseline blood tests: Haemoglobin 131 g/L, normal inflammatory markers, LDH 743 IU/L (raised), AFP 4 kU/L (normal), and β-hCG 3 IU/L (upper limit of normal 2 IU/L).
Testicular ultrasound: Grossly enlarged testicle with a heterogeneous sonographic appearance, normal architecture not perceptible, and chaotic intratesticular perfusion on colour Doppler.
Contrast-enhanced CT of the thorax, abdomen and pelvis: Soft-tissue mass in the left testicle extending through the left spermatic cord as a continuous soft-tissue column, most likely within the left gonadal vein, to the level of the left kidney, with a further large soft-tissue suprarenal mass.
FDG-PET scan: The left testicular mass, the soft tissue extending from it, and the left suprarenal mass were FDG avid.
Ultrasound-guided core biopsy of the left testicular mass: Cores highly suspicious for high-grade diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, non-follicle centre type (ABC).

cases.case_summary: A 28-year-old man is admitted to the emergency department with a tonic-clonic seizure, left arm weakness, weakness of both legs, two months of gait disturbance, and a fever of 38°C.
cases.full_text:
A 28-year-old man is admitted to the emergency department with a tonic-clonic seizure, left arm weakness, weakness of both legs, two months of gait disturbance, and a fever of 38°C.
HIV-1 testing and baseline laboratories: HIV-1 diagnosed three months earlier; CD4+ T-cell count 669 cells/μL, viral load 23,800 c/mL, CDC stage A1, and not yet on antiretroviral therapy.
Mental status and limb examination: Confusional state, somnolence, hypoprosexia, and complex visual hallucinations. Left arm strength 3/5, symmetric lower-limb paresis 2/5 with symmetrically increased myotatic reflexes, and Babinski sign absent.
Remainder of the neurological examination: Cranial nerves, optic fundus, and papilla without alteration; sensory examination normal; no meningeal signs, abnormal movements, or ataxia.
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis: Clear fluid; protein 27 mg/dl; glucose 74 mg/dl with serum glucose 90 mg/dl; white blood cell count 20 cells/mm3 (54% lymphocytes); no malignant cells and no oligoclonal bands.
CSF infection studies and Toxoplasma serology: CSF cryptococcal antigen, M. tuberculosis PCR, VDRL, bacterial cultures, Gram stain, and Ziehl-Neelsen stain negative. Serum Toxoplasma gondii IgG negative.
Brain MRI: Lesions mainly affecting the centrum semiovale, frontal lobe, and left parietal lobe; hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted and FLAIR images, restricted diffusion, and a parietal ring-enhancing lesion after IV gadolinium.

cases.case_summary: A 72-year-old man is admitted with right flank pain and massive hematuria with clot retention.
cases.full_text:
A 72-year-old man is admitted with right flank pain and massive hematuria with clot retention.
Smoking history: Heavy smoker
History of trauma, recent medical intervention, or lithiasis: No reported history of trauma, recent medical intervention, or known lithiasis
Bleeding-disorder and medication history: Denied any bleeding disorder and was not taking any medications
Blood pressure, blood count, biochemistry, and coagulation: Blood pressure, blood count, biochemical parameters, and coagulation parameters were normal
Contrast-enhanced CT of the kidneys: Small soft-tissue mass in the right renal pelvis that did not significantly enhance; no dilatation of the affected renal unit and no urinary tract lithiasis or other pathology
Cystoscopy and upper tract cytology: Both negative for a high-grade bladder tumor
Retrograde study of the right ureter and pelvicaliceal system: No filling defect in the right renal pelvis or calyces
Selective right renal arteriography: Area of tortuous, coiled vascular channels with early filling of the renal vein within two seconds after the start of the injection

cases.case_summary: A 38-year-old woman was referred from the general outpatient clinic with a one-month history of recurrent difficulty breathing, chest pain, headaches, blurring of vision, and dizziness, and a blood pressure of 260/150 mmHg.
cases.full_text:
A 38-year-old woman was referred from the general outpatient clinic with a one-month history of recurrent difficulty breathing, chest pain, headaches, blurring of vision, and dizziness, and a blood pressure of 260/150 mmHg.
Past medical history: Diagnosed as hypertensive five years before presentation and not compliant with antihypertensive medications. No known family history of hypertension.
Presenting symptoms: One-month history of recurrent difficulty in breathing, chest pain, recurrent headaches, blurring of vision, and dizziness, with blood pressure 260/150 mmHg.
Associated symptoms: Orthopnoea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, no cough, mild central chest pain, and progressively worsening bilateral leg swelling with reduced urine volume.
Cardiorespiratory examination: Respiratory rate 50 cycles/minute, reduced breath sounds in the left lower lung zones, and bibasal fine crepitations. Pulse 118 beats/minute, normal volume and regular, with clinical evidence of arterial wall thickening. Blood pressure 220/120 mmHg, a fourth heart sound, and a loud aortic component of the second heart sound.
Serum chemistry: Predialysis creatinine 900 μmol/L (reference 53–115), urea 30 mmol/L (reference 2.1–7.1), sodium 136 mmol/L, potassium 4.0 mmol/L, chloride 98 mmol/L, and bicarbonate 28 mmol/L.
Urinalysis: Proteinuria (++) and no haematuria.
Renal ultrasound and renal artery Doppler: Right kidney 8.63 × 4.59 × 5.07 cm with loss of corticomedullary differentiation; right renal artery velocity 73.9 cm/second and resistive index 0.9. The upper margin of the left kidney appeared intrathoracic and could not be well deciphered; the left kidney was hypoechoic with complete loss of corticomedullary differentiation, and left renal artery Doppler velocity was 195 cm/min.
Abdominal CT: Scanogram showed a left intrathoracic well-marginated upper-border mass obscuring the left hemidiaphragm medially and the cardiac apex. Contiguous slices showed the left kidney in an abnormal location in the left hemithorax, between the cardiac silhouette and the spleen. The right kidney was normally located with major blood vessels appearing normal, and the left kidney was slightly bigger than the right.

cases.case_summary: An 8-year-old girl is admitted to the emergency department with 10 days of left-sided ear pain, ear discharge, and hearing loss, and with strabismus and binocular double vision that began on the day of admission.
cases.full_text:
An 8-year-old girl is admitted to the emergency department with 10 days of left-sided ear pain, ear discharge, and hearing loss, and with strabismus and binocular double vision that began on the day of admission.
Presenting symptoms: Ten-day history of left-sided otalgia, otorrhea, and ipsilateral hearing loss, with new-onset strabismus and binocular diplopia since the day of admission.
Associated symptoms: Vomiting since the previous night, with no headache or ocular pain.
Physical examination: Suppurative left-sided acute otitis media, bilateral conductive hearing loss on tuning-fork acumetry, ipsilateral abducens nerve palsy, and a fever of 38.0°C.
Trigeminal sensory and meningeal examination: Light touch and pinprick sensation preserved in the trigeminal distribution; no other focal neurological deficit; meningeal signs negative.
Ophthalmologic examination: Left lateral rectus paralysis, with normal biomicroscopy, fundoscopy, and normal visual acuity.
Blood count and C-reactive protein: White blood cell count 26200/μL with 24500 neutrophils/μL (93.4%) and C-reactive protein 88.8 mg/L.
MRI of the mastoid and petrous apex: Diffuse inflammatory enhancement in the left mastoid air cells and petrous apex, with extraosseous extension to the petroclival suture and to dura adjacent to the clivus and petrous apex on the same side.
MRI of the carotid canal and cavernous sinus: Intense enhancement in the left carotid canal with about 50% stenosis of the petrous, lacerum, and cavernous segments, plus intense enhancement and swelling of the cavernous sinus.

cases.case_summary: A previously healthy 44-year-old man was admitted with five months of progressively worsening fatigue.
cases.full_text:
A previously healthy 44-year-old man was admitted with five months of progressively worsening fatigue.
Physical examination: Temperature 98.6°F, blood pressure 159/92 mmHg, and heart rate 100/min. Cardiovascular and pulmonary examinations were unremarkable. Left upper quadrant tenderness was present, with a firm spleen palpable below the umbilicus. No rash and no cervical or axillary lymphadenopathy.
Complete blood count and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: Hemoglobin 6.7 g/dL, hematocrit 21.4%, MCV 82.3 μm3, white blood cell count 3.93 × 10^9/L, platelet count 254 × 10^9/L, and ESR 93 mm/h. Peripheral blood smear within normal limits.
Serum calcium and renal function tests: Calcium 13.7 mg/dL, BUN 33 mg/dL, and serum creatinine 2.39 mg/dL.
Abdominal sonogram: Diffusely heterogeneous spleen measuring 30 cm in length. Kidneys enlarged with normal echogenicity, right kidney 13 cm and left kidney 15.5 cm.
Chest radiograph and CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis: Mildly enlarged paraaortic, mesenteric, and bilateral iliac chain lymph nodes. Chest radiograph unremarkable. Diffuse mediastinal, lower cervical, and axillary adenopathy.
Vitamin D, parathyroid hormone, and screening tests: Elevated 1,25(OH)2 vitamin D with low parathyroid hormone. Anti-nuclear antibody, HIV test, monospot test, and PPD were negative.
Excisional biopsy of a left inguinal lymph node: The node was extensively involved by small compact nonnecrotizing granulomas. GMS stain showed no fungal organisms and AFB stain showed no acid-fast organisms. No morphologic or immunophenotypic evidence of malignancy.
Serum angiotensin-converting enzyme: 73 U/L (reference range 9–67).

cases.case_summary: A 50-year-old man had dull, long-lasting pain in the left dorsolateral chest.
cases.full_text:
A 50-year-old man had dull, long-lasting pain in the left dorsolateral chest.
History of fever, night sweats, or weight loss: No history of fever, night sweats, or weight loss.
Physical and neurological examination: Limited movement at the waist, with no motor or sensor abnormalities; neurological examination normal.
Laboratory tests: Blood cell count, serum electrolytes, renal and liver function tests, ESR, and CRP were normal.
CT scan: Widening of the left T10 costovertebral joint with scalloping and mild sclerosis of the left aspect of the T10 vertebral body, partially involving the left pedicle and the adjacent costal bone.
18-FDG PET/CT: No significant tracer uptake.
MRI: Low signal on T1-weighted images and high signal on T2-weighted fat-saturated images, with bone marrow edema of the T10 body and pedicle and adjacent costal bone, partially extending to the left neural arch without spinal canal invasion, and contrast enhancement after gadolinium.
Fluoroscopy-guided needle biopsy of T10: Fibrous/myxoid tissue with reactive lymphocytes and plasma cells and rare histiocytic elements.
CD1a immunostain: Numerous Langerhans cells.

cases.case_summary: A 72-year-old man presented to the emergency department with four days of abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, including an episode of confusion and slurred speech.
cases.full_text:
A 72-year-old man presented to the emergency department with four days of abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, including an episode of confusion and slurred speech.
Prior trauma: A fall four months earlier fractured several ribs on the left side.
Skin examination: Petechiae along the inner left thigh.
Platelet count: 28×10^9/L
Contrast CT of the abdomen: The entire spleen was non-enhancing.
Coagulation studies: Klaus fibrinogen 4.30 g/L, INR 1.1, and PTT 26 seconds.
Peripheral blood smear: Some evidence of mild schistocytes on day three of admission.
Recent wound and animal contact: Several days before presentation he cut his hand while repairing an automobile, and shortly afterward his dog licked the wound.
Blood culture gene sequencing: Capnocytophaga canimorsus was isolated.

cases.case_summary: A healthy 13-year-old boy was brought to the emergency department with mild dyspnea, chest pain on exertion, and a new cardiac murmur.
cases.full_text:
A healthy 13-year-old boy was brought to the emergency department with mild dyspnea, chest pain on exertion, and a new cardiac murmur.
Symptom timeline: Symptoms began three weeks before the emergency visit and worsened with intense physical activity.
Cardiac and abdominal examination: Regular heart rate and rhythm with a few extrasystolic beats, normal S1 and S2, grade 3/6 systolic murmur loudest at the pulmonary focus, no gallops or rubs, symmetrical peripheral pulses, and mild hepatomegaly.
Blood tests: Hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL, GPT-transaminase 43 U/L, and NT-proBNP 4019 pg/mL. Coagulation parameters, renal function tests, C-reactive protein, and high-sensitivity troponin were normal.
Electrocardiogram: Sinus rhythm with normal PR and QTc intervals, right bundle block with ventricular repolarization abnormalities in the right leads, and isolated monomorphic premature ventricular contractions, often in bigeminy.
Echocardiogram: Rounded, lobulated 3.5 × 4 cm mass with clear margins and inhomogeneous content, adherent to the infundibular septum by a pedicle. Right ventricular outflow maximum instantaneous systolic gradient 80 mmHg, with the pulmonary valve spared. Right atrial area 23.5 cm²; right ventricular telediastolic area 23 cm² and telesystolic area 19 cm²; fractional area change 18.6%.
Contrast CT: Heterogeneously enhancing soft-tissue mass occupying the right ventricular outflow tract, with no evidence of pulmonary embolization.
Intraoperative inspection: A 4 cm × 4 cm gelatinous mass with a pedicle arising in the right outflow a few millimeters from the pulmonary valve and projecting toward the valve, obstructing the right ventricular outflow.
Pathology of the excised mass: Whitish ovoid nodule, 3 cm in diameter, with a smooth surface. Histology showed a myxoid background with mostly loose, multifocally denser proliferation of single cells or cords, a low mitotic index, and no atypia.

cases.case_summary: A 6-year-old Caucasian girl is admitted from the emergency room with red, sensitive, swollen eyelids after 5 days of fever up to 39.5 °C and 2 weeks of clear tearing from the right eye.
cases.full_text:
A 6-year-old Caucasian girl is admitted from the emergency room with red, sensitive, swollen eyelids after 5 days of fever up to 39.5 °C and 2 weeks of clear tearing from the right eye.
Recent nasal symptoms: Chronic nasal obstruction, noisy breathing, and rhinolalia for 4–6 weeks, with purulent anterior rhinorrhea for 7 days.
Periorbital examination: Right periorbital swelling, predominant on the upper eyelid, with no ocular discharge.
Nasal mucosa and neck examination: Swollen nasal mucosa and bilateral neck lymphadenopathy, predominant on the right.
Abdominal and throat examination: No organomegaly, and the throat was not inflammatory.
Blood analysis: Normal white blood cell count with a left shift, C-reactive protein 22 mg/l, and normal procalcitonin.
Cerebral computed tomography: Right preseptal infiltration and an ipsilateral well-delimited collection measuring 11 × 18 × 13 mm with enhanced borders; no signs of acute sinusitis or intracranial complications.
Bacterial cultures and MRSA screening: Blood cultures, eye-discharge swabs, and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus screening were negative.
Epstein–Barr virus serology: Positive, with highly elevated immunoglobulin G and immunoglobulin M antibodies.

draft.opening: A 16-year-old girl was referred to the neurology department with bilateral horizontal gaze palsy that started suddenly and developed overnight.

findings.name: Sensory symptom history
findings.result: Paresthesias in both feet for 2 months, spreading over 2 weeks to the trunk at the umbilicus, and similar paresthesias in both hands about 1 year earlier.
findings.quote: The patient also reported a history of paresthesia in both of her feet since 2 months ago, which had progressed in the course duration of 2 weeks reaching her trunk at the level of the umbilicus. She experienced similar symptoms in both of her hands approximately 1 year ago.

findings.name: Eye movement and pupil examination
findings.result: Complete bilateral horizontal gaze palsy, with vertical gaze preserved except for slightly slowed saccades. Pupils midsize and reactive. No nystagmus, diplopia, or blurred vision.
findings.quote: the patient had complete bilateral horizontal gaze palsy in the horizontal plane while vertical gaze was normal, aside from slightly decreased velocity of saccadic movements. Pupils were midsize and reactive, and nystagmus, diplopia or blurry vision were not found.

findings.name: Facial nerve examination
findings.result: Mild bilateral peripheral facial nerve palsy.
findings.quote: Mild bilateral peripheral facial nerve palsy was also presented in the physical exam.

findings.name: Limb motor and reflex examination
findings.result: Hyperreflexia in all four limbs without clonus, downgoing plantar reflexes, and no loss of muscle strength. No spasticity or ataxia.
findings.quote: Hyperreflexia in all four limbs was detectable without clonus, plantar reflexes were down going, and muscle forces were not reduced. There were no apparent signs of spasticity and ataxia.

findings.name: Brain MRI
findings.result: Multiple hyperintense subcortical and periventricular lesions on FLAIR and T2-weighted images, with bilateral pontine involvement of the paramedian pontine reticular formation anterior to the cerebral aqueduct.
findings.quote: Magnetic resonance imaging indicated multiple hyperintense subcortical, and periventricular lesions visible on the fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) and T2-weighted images, in addition to bilaterally involving PPRF at the level of the pons, anterior to the cerebral aqueduct

findings.name: Spinal cord MRI
findings.result: Two hyperintense lesions on sagittal images, one at C7 and one adjacent to T4.
findings.quote: Two hyperintense lesions were also presented in the sagittal sections of the spinal MRI, one at the level of C7 and the other adjacent to T4.

findings.name: Gadolinium-enhanced MRI
findings.result: The paramedian pontine reticular formation lesions did not enhance. The T4 thoracic cord lesion enhanced.
findings.quote: After gadolinium injection, the PPRF lesions were not enhanced, however, T4 thoracic spine lesion was enhanced.

findings.name: Aquaporin-4 and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody tests
findings.result: Both negative.
findings.quote: Anti-aquaporin 4 (AQP4) and anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) antibodies were accomplished in order to rule out neuromyelitis optica (NMO) and both tests were negative.

findings.name: Earlier SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR
findings.result: COVID-19 was confirmed by RT-PCR, and he remained asymptomatic afterward.
