findings.name: Recent isolation history
findings.result: The febrile illness with rash began two days after he completed 14-day home isolation.
findings.quote: two days after completing 14-day home isolation

findings.name: Fever and rash
findings.result: Mild intermittent fever with chills occurred with a simultaneous maculopapular abdominal rash of lesions 0.5–2 mm; the rash was non-blanching, non-pruritic, and non-tender and rapidly desquamated into annular plaques with satellite lesions.
findings.quote: The onset of symptoms was described as mild, intermittent fever associated with chills. A maculopapular rash with lesions of varying sizes (0.5–2 mm) appeared on the abdomen simultaneously with the onset of fever. The rash was non-blanching, non-pruritic, and non-tender to palpation, and it desquamated rapidly into annular plaques with satellite lesions

findings.name: Symptom review
findings.result: Several episodes of vomiting and diarrhea without abdominal pain; no headache, myalgia, arthralgia, bleeding, mucosal involvement, coryza, sore throat, or cough.
findings.quote: There was an additional history of having several episodes of vomiting and diarrhea during the first few days of illness, but he denied experiencing abdominal pain. There was no history of headache, myalgia, arthralgia, bleeding, or any mucosal involvement. In addition, there was no history of any kind of respiratory symptoms, including coryza, sore throat, or cough.

findings.name: Examination at presentation
findings.result: Conscious and lucid, with blood pressure 84/52 mmHg, a feeble regular pulse at 137 beats/min, cool lower extremities, undetectable distal pulses, and prolonged capillary fill time. Temperature 38.2 °C, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 99–100% in room air, distant heart sounds, normal breath sounds, and no neurological deficit.
findings.quote: On examination, the patient was conscious and lucid despite being in shock. The blood pressure was 84/52 mmHg, and the pulse was feeble and regular at 137 beats/min. The lower extremities were cool to the touch, with undetectable distal peripheral pulses and a prolonged capillary fill time. The oral temperature was 38.2 °C, and the respiratory rate was 20 breaths/min, with an oxygen saturation of 99–100% in room air. The tachycardia and distant heart sounds were audible with normal breath sounds through auscultation, and there was no neurological deficit.

findings.name: Inflammatory markers
findings.result: Inflammatory markers were markedly elevated; specific analyte values are not given in the narrative.
findings.quote: a marked elevation of inflammatory markers

findings.name: Echocardiography
findings.result: Global left ventricular hypokinesia, mitral and tricuspid valve regurgitation, dilation of all four chambers, pericardial effusion, and ejection fraction less than 30%.
findings.quote: Echocardiography showed global left ventricular hypokinesia with a moderate left ventricular dysfunction. In addition to this, there was mitral and tricuspid valve regurgitation, with the dilation of all four chambers of the heart, pericardial effusion, and an ejection fraction (EF) less than 30%.

findings.name: Dengue testing
findings.result: Dengue IgM was positive by ELISA; rapid tests for dengue IgM, IgG, and NS1 were negative.
findings.quote: Despite the ELISA positive test results for dengue IgM in this case, the rapid test kit results for dengue IgM, IgG, and NS1 were all negative.

findings.name: Family history
findings.result: No family history of genitourinary malignancy or renal cancer, and no history of skin or uterine leiomyomas.
findings.quote: The patient did not have a family history of genitourinary malignancy, including no family history of renal cancers; there was also no history of skin or uterine leiomyomas.

findings.name: Prior renal imaging
findings.result: Mild bilateral cystic disease.
findings.quote: mild bilateral cystic disease identified on previous imaging

findings.name: Surveillance renal imaging
findings.result: Interval increase in size of an endophytic right interpolar Bosniak III renal cyst.
findings.quote: interval increase in size of an endophytic right interpolar Bosniak III renal cyst on surveillance imaging

findings.name: Renal mass size
findings.result: 1.9 × 2.0 × 1.6 cm renal mass.
findings.quote: 1.9 × 2.0 × 1.6cm renal mass

findings.name: Histologic architecture
findings.result: Well-circumscribed mass of cysts ranging from small, closely packed tubules to larger simple cysts, separated by fibrous stroma, with some papillary architecture.
findings.quote: a well-circumscribed renal mass consisting of cysts, which varied in size from small, more closely packed tubules to larger simple cysts, separated by fibrous stroma, with some areas demonstrating papillary architecture

findings.name: Tumor cell morphology
findings.result: Cyst lining was predominantly a single layer and occasionally multiple layers of cells with variable eosinophilic cytoplasm resembling oncocytic cells; hobnail cells, focal intracytoplasmic vacuoles, and prominent grade 3 nucleoli were present.
findings.quote: The cysts were predominantly lined by a single layer and occasionally by multiple layers of cells with variable amounts of eosinophilic cytoplasm resembling oncocytic cells (Figures 2(a) – 2(c) ). In areas, the tumor cells had a hobnail appearance and focally they contained intracytoplasmic vacuoles. Nucleoli were prominent (grade 3)

findings.name: Stromal histology
findings.result: Ovarian-type stroma was absent.
findings.quote: Ovarian-type stroma seen in cystic nephromas, seen almost exclusively in women, was absent.

findings.name: Immunohistochemistry
findings.result: Focally positive for CK7 and 34-beta-E12; diffusely positive for AMACR and vimentin; fumarate hydratase loss not detected; weakly positive for RCC; negative for S100 protein and c-kit; Ki-67 proliferative activity was low.
findings.quote: the tumor cells were focally positive for CK7 and 34-beta-E12 and diffusely positive for AMACR and vimentin. Fumarate hydratase loss was not detected. The cells were weakly positive for RCC, but negative for S100 protein and c-kit. The proliferative activity in the Ki-67 stain was low

findings.result: Pitting edema of the left lower extremity, strong peripheral pulses, and a soft, nondistended abdomen.

findings.name: Stool pathogen testing

findings.name: Chest radiograph

findings.name: Upper endoscopy mucosal biopsies

findings.quote: mucosal biopsies were obtained from the esophagus, stomach, duodenum and jejunum. Histological exam revealed eosinophilic-predominant mucosal inflammatory infiltrates in all biopsied specimens as shown in Fig. 1 . Helicobacter Pylori was negative. No villous abnormality, cryptitis or crypt abscesses were identified.

findings.name: Duodenal biopsy
findings.result: Markedly increased eosinophils, greater than 20 per high-power field, in the lamina propria, with focal epithelial involvement.

encounter.cutoff_quote: In addition to the COVID-19 pneumonia, a primary VZV coinfection with possible pulmonary involvement and ventilator-associated multibacterial tracheobronchitis with Staphylococcus aureus , E. cloacae , and Serratia marcescens were diagnosed.

findings.name: Admission history
findings.result: 48-year-old Caucasian man with traumatic epidural hematoma and subarachnoid bleeding, intubated after rapid neurological deterioration and transferred for neurosurgical intervention.
findings.quote: A 48-year-old Caucasian male with traumatic epidural hematoma and subarachnoid bleeding was transferred, after rapid neurological deterioration necessitating intubation, from another hospital to a tertiary university hospital for neurosurgical intervention.

findings.name: Symptoms and exposure before admission
findings.result: Fever and nonproductive cough for 3–4 days before admission, and direct contact with a person who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2.
findings.quote: The patient had a history of preexisting fever and nonproductive cough over a period of 3–4 days prior to admission and had direct contact with a person who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2.

findings.name: Admission SARS-CoV-2 PCR
findings.result: Positive.
findings.quote: A SARS-CoV-2 polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test performed upon admission was positive.

findings.name: Skin examination
findings.result: Maculopapular erythematous exanthema predominantly on the trunk and upper and lower extremities; mucosae, palms, and soles spared.
findings.quote: a maculopapular erythematous exanthema predominantly on the trunk and upper and lower extremities was noted. Mucosae, palmar surfaces of hands, and plantar surfaces of feet were spared

findings.name: Course after the exanthema appeared
findings.result: The exanthema progressed to a papulovesicular rash, with severe septic shock requiring volume substitution and high-dose vasoactive agents and progressive respiratory failure with rapidly rising oxygen demand.
findings.quote: over the following days the exanthema progressed to a papulovesicular rash. The patient developed severe septic shock requiring volume substitution and high-dose vasoactive agents, as well as progressive respiratory failure with rapidly rising oxygen demand.

findings.name: Cutaneous vesicle swab PCR
findings.result: Positive for varicella zoster virus; negative for herpes simplex virus types 1–2 and SARS-CoV-2.
findings.quote: A PCR from a swab taken from a cutaneous vesicular lesion was positive for VZV and negative for herpes simplex virus types 1–2 and SARS-CoV-2.

findings.name: Varicella zoster virus serology
findings.result: VZV IgM index >2.3 (negative <1.0) and VZV IgG 61 mlU/ml (negative <150); the paired earlier result was recorded as not obtained.
findings.quote: VZV IgM, index (negative < 1.0) – > 2.3 VZV IgG, mlU/ml (negative < 150) – 61

findings.name: Tracheal secretion testing
findings.result: Polymicrobial bacterial flora with Staphylococcus aureus, Enterobacter cloacae, and Serratia marcescens; VZV PCR positive at 4700 GEq/ml.
findings.quote: Microbiological testing of the tracheal secretion revealed a polymicrobial bacterial flora with Staphylococcus aureus , Enterobacter cloacae , and Serratia marcescens . In addition, a specific PCR test was positive for VZV (4700 GEq/ml).

draft.opening: In July 2009, she presented with right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and fevers as high as 102.4°F.
draft.opening_quote: In July of 2009, the patient once again presented to an outside hospital with right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and fevers of up to 102. 4 °F.
draft.diagnosis_quote: Based on the presumptive diagnosis of hepatic bartonellosis

encounter.start: July 2009 presentation with right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and fever
encounter.cutoff: PCR of formalin-fixed liver resection tissue amplified B. henselae 16S rRNA
encounter.cutoff_quote: A sample of formalin-fixed liver tissue from the initial liver resection was sent to the University of Arkansas for PCR testing. Using previously validated assay conditions, a 153 bp fragment of the B. henselae 16S rRNA gene was amplified, and confirmed by Southern blot hybridization

findings.name: Liver resection histopathology
findings.result: Florid necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with pseudotumor formation
findings.quote: Histopathological studies of the resection specimen showed florid necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with pseudotumor formation

findings.name: Bartonella immunofluorescence assay
findings.result: Negative for Bartonella henselae and Bartonella quintana
findings.quote: IFA assays for Bartonella henselae and Bartonella quintana were negative.

findings.name: Presenting symptoms
findings.result: Right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and fevers up to 102.4°F
findings.quote: right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and fevers of up to 102. 4 °F

findings.name: Abdominal CT
findings.result: Several low-attenuation lesions involving both segments of the liver, the largest measuring 4.1 × 2.9 cm
findings.quote: An abdominal CT revealed several low attenuation lesions involving both segments of the liver, with the largest one measuring 4.1 × 2.9 cm

findings.name: Physical examination
findings.result: Afebrile, no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly, and right upper quadrant tenderness without rebound tenderness or guarding
findings.quote: the patient was afebrile. There was no lymphadenopathy or hepato-splenomegaly. Her right upper quadrant was tender to palpation without rebound tenderness or guarding.

findings.name: Percutaneous liver biopsy
findings.result: Extensive granulomatous hepatitis with occasional fibrin rings and background mixed microvesicular and macrovesicular steatosis
findings.quote: revealed extensive granulomatous hepatitis with occasional fibrin rings, with a background of mixed, micro- and macro-vesicular steatosis.

findings.name: Steiner silver stain of liver tissue
findings.result: Negative for spirochetes and bacteria, including Bartonella species
findings.quote: Steiner silver stains for spirochetes and bacteria - including Bartonella sp.- were negative.

findings.name: 16S rRNA PCR of formalin-fixed liver resection tissue
findings.result: A 153 bp fragment of the B. henselae 16S rRNA gene was amplified and confirmed by Southern blot hybridization
findings.quote: a 153 bp fragment of the B. henselae 16S rRNA gene was amplified, and confirmed by Southern blot hybridization

findings.name: Illness 8 weeks before presentation

findings.name: Nasal COVID-19 polymerase chain reaction

findings.name: Blood count and serum chemistries

draft.opening: A 71-year-old man was transferred from a long-term acute care facility with a 2-day history of right wrist and hand pain and swelling.
draft.opening_quote: A 71-year-old man with a medical history of coronary artery disease requiring PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention) years ago, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, gout, and benign prostatic hyperplasia was transferred to our facility from a long-term acute care facility (LTAC) with a 2-day history of right wrist and hand pain and swelling.
draft.diagnosis_quote: This patient developed right forearm compartment syndrome with sensorimotor function loss due to an expanding hematoma

encounter.start: Transfer from long-term acute care with a 2-day history of right wrist and hand pain and swelling
encounter.cutoff: Clinical diagnosis established on repeat examination, before fasciotomy
encounter.cutoff_quote: Compartment pressures were not measured, since the diagnosis was established clinically.

findings.name: Prior arterial and venous access
findings.result: Frequent arterial blood gas sampling from both radial arteries, multiple venous blood draws, and peripheral intravenous placements on both hands and arms; no arterial line was placed.
findings.quote: He had undergone frequent ABG sampling from both radial arteries, as well as multiple venous blood draws and peripheral intravenous line placements on both the hands and arms, though he never had an arterial line placed.

findings.name: Home medications
findings.result: Aspirin, atorvastatin, carvedilol, lisinopril, and as-needed sublingual nitroglycerin.
findings.quote: His home medications included aspirin, atorvastatin, carvedilol, lisinopril, and as needed sublingual nitroglycerin.

findings.name: Transfer medications
findings.result: Meropenem, famotidine, furosemide, and enoxaparin 90 mg (1 mg/kg bodyweight) every 12 hours subcutaneously.
findings.quote: Transfer medications included meropenem, famotidine, furosemide, and enoxaparin 90 mg (1 mg/kg bodyweight) every 12 hours subcutaneously.

findings.name: Reported bleeding symptoms
findings.result: Easy bruising and bleeding, along with fatigue, shortness of breath, and generalized weakness.
findings.quote: He complained of fatigue, shortness of breath, generalized weakness, and easy bruising and bleeding.

findings.name: Admission examination of the right wrist and hand
findings.result: Mildly tender and swollen, with bruising on the inside of the right wrist. Radial and ulnar pulses were palpable, sensation and motor strength were normal, and the fingers were cool to touch.
findings.quote: His right wrist and hand were mildly tender and swollen with some bruising noted on the inside of the right wrist. The right radial and ulnar pulses were palpable. He had normal sensation and motor strength in the hand and wrist. The fingers of the right hand were cool to touch.

findings.name: Right arm arterial duplex
findings.result: Patent arterial vasculature of the right arm and digits.
findings.quote: Arterial duplex studies demonstrated patent arterial vasculature of the right arm and digits.

findings.name: Repeat right forearm and hand examination at 20 hours
findings.result: New numbness and tingling in the right thumb, index, and middle fingers; marked distal forearm tenderness; increased swelling with a forearm hematoma; radial pulse no longer palpable; newly diminished palmar sensation of the first through third fingers; unable to move the right first three digits.
findings.quote: 20 hours after admission, the patient reported new onset numbness and tingling in his right thumb, index, and middle fingers. On exam, he had significant tenderness to palpation in the distal volar and dorsal forearm just proximal to the wrist, and the right forearm and hand were significantly more swollen than only hours earlier, with development of a significant hematoma in the right forearm; the radial pulse was no longer palpable. He had newly diminished sensation over the palmar aspect of the D1–3 fingers in a median nerve distribution, and he was unable to move his right first three digits.

encounter.start: presentation with progressive four-limb weakness and urinary retention
encounter.cutoff: Ziehl-Neelsen stain of the paravertebral and breast aspirates
encounter.cutoff_quote: ZN (Ziehl-Neelsen) stain of both lesions showed presence of acid fast bacilli ( Figure 7 ) which was suggestive of tubercular lesion.

findings.name: Recent fever and neck pain
findings.result: Low-grade fever for about one week two months earlier, which subsided spontaneously, followed by persistent dull aching neck pain and gradually progressive quadriparesis.
findings.quote: Two months back she had a preceding history of low grade fever for about one week which subsided spontaneously but she developed a persistent dull aching neck pain along with a gradually progressive quadriparesis.

findings.name: Neurological examination
findings.result: Grade 3 power in both lower limbs and grade 4 power in both upper limbs, spasticity with exaggerated deep tendon reflexes in all four limbs, bilateral extensor plantar responses, and hypoesthesia of both lower limbs without a definite sensory level.
findings.quote: Neurological examination revealed grade 3 power in both lower limbs and grade 4 power in both upper limbs, spasticity of all four limbs with exaggerated deep tendon reflexes in all 4 limbs, and bilateral extensor type of plantar response and hypoesthesia of both lower limbs but there was no definite sensory level.

findings.name: Hemoglobin, leukocyte count, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
findings.result: Hemoglobin 8.1 g/dL, total leukocyte count 8,000/mm3, and ESR 42 mm in the first hour.
findings.quote: Her routine blood investigation revealed a hemoglobin level of 8.1 g/dL, total leucocyte count was 8,000/mm 3 , and ESR (erythrocyte sedimentation rate) was 42 mm in 1st hour.

findings.name: Chest radiograph
findings.result: Expansile lesion involving the right 4th rib.
findings.quote: Her chest X-ray showed an expansile lesion involving right 4th rib

findings.name: Magnetic resonance imaging of the cervical spine
findings.result: Altered marrow signal with erosion of C5 to D1, intraspinal extension and elevation of the posterior longitudinal ligament compressing the thecal sac and spinal cord; intervertebral discs of normal height and signal intensity.
findings.quote: MRI of spine revealed altered marrow signal intensity with erosion of C5 to D1 vertebrae. There was intraspinal extension of the disease process with elevation of posterior longitudinal ligament between C5 and D1 levels causing compression of thecal sac and spinal cord. The intervertebral discs were of normal height and signal intensity

findings.name: Magnetic resonance imaging of the dorsal and lumbar spine
findings.result: Altered marrow signal and abnormal soft tissue involving D6, D7, D9, D10, L2 to L5, and the sacrum, with pedicle involvement at D10 and L5, thecal sac compression at D6 and in the sacrum, and large pre- and paravertebral soft tissue at the dorsal level and presacral space.
findings.quote: MRI of dorsal and lumbar spine showed altered marrow signal intensity with abnormal soft tissue lesion involving D6, D7, D9, D10, and L2 to L5 vertebrae and sacrum. Pedicles at D10 and L5 level are also involved. Intraspinal extension with thecal sac compression is seen at the level of D6 vertebrae and in sacrum. Large pre- and paravertebral soft tissue element are seen at dorsal level and presacral space

findings.name: Breast ultrasonography
findings.result: Hypoechoic heterogeneous right breast mass measuring 3.5 × 2.3 cm with echogenic foci; right axillary lymph nodes enlarged, the largest 2 × 0.8 cm; left breast normal.
findings.quote: hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass lesion involving right breast measuring 3.5 × 2.3 cm ( Figure 5 ) with echogenic foci within it. Few enlarged axillary lymph nodes are noted on right side, the largest of which was 2 × 0.8 cm USG of left breast was normal.

findings.name: Fine-needle aspiration cytology and Ziehl-Neelsen stain
findings.result: Aspirates from the paravertebral collection and right breast lesion showed degenerated inflammatory cells in a necrotic background, without malignant cells or granuloma; Ziehl-Neelsen stain showed acid-fast bacilli in both lesions.
findings.quote: CT (computed tomography) guided FNAC (fine needle aspiration cytology) from paravertebral collection and USG guided FNAC from right breast lesion ( Figure 6 ) both of which showed degenerated inflammatory cells in a necrotic background without any presence of malignant cell or granuloma. However, ZN (Ziehl-Neelsen) stain of both lesions showed presence of acid fast bacilli

findings.name: Recent staging CT and anticoagulation
findings.result: One month earlier, CT showed stable malignant disease, new bilateral lower-lobe pulmonary emboli, and left common femoral vein thrombosis; she was treated with once-daily therapeutic-dose dalteparin.
findings.quote: 1 month earlier a routine CT staging examination had shown stable malignant disease, but it also found new bilateral lower lobe pulmonary emboli when compared to previous imaging ( Figures 1a, b, 2a and b ) and thrombosis of the left common femoral vein. findings.result: Normal at 468 × 10^9/L.

findings.result: 84% while receiving 2 L of oxygen per minute.

findings.name: Admission platelet count

findings.name: Blood film and repeat platelet counts
findings.result: Some platelet clumping and fibrin stranding; repeat counts confirmed a genuine thrombocytopenia.
findings.quote: A blood film showed some platelet clumping and fibrin stranding, nonetheless multiple repeat platelet count measurements confirmed a genuine thrombocytopaenia.

findings.name: Admission CT of the thorax, abdomen and pelvis
findings.result: Progression of pulmonary emboli with new thrombus in the left and right main pulmonary arteries, no radiological features of right heart strain, and new mural hypodensities in the thoracic and upper abdominal aorta reported as extensive acute non-occlusive mural thrombi.
findings.quote: a repeat CT thorax, abdomen and pelvis showed progression of the previously identified pulmonary emboli, with new thrombi seen within the left and right main pulmonary arteries ( Figure 1c ), but with no radiological features to suggest right heart strain. New mural hypodensities were also identified in the thoracic and upper abdominal aorta in keeping with extensive acute non-occlusive mural thrombi ( Figure 2c ).

draft.opening: An 18-month-old child is brought in with intermittent spiking fever, constipation, and abdominal distension since 1 month after birth, with gradual onset of the distension.
draft.opening_quote: An 18-month-old child who came with the complaints of intermittent spiking fever, constipation, and abdominal distension since 1 month after birth. The distension of abdomen was gradual in onset.
draft.diagnosis_quote: The diagnosis of hereditary tyrosinemia Type 1 was hence confirmed.

encounter.start: presentation at age 18 months
encounter.cutoff: urinary organic acid result during the same diagnostic workup
encounter.cutoff_quote: urinary organic acid were then requested which determined high level of succinylacetone. The diagnosis of hereditary tyrosinemia Type 1 was hence confirmed.

findings.name: Family history
findings.result: A sister had a similar illness; the parents did not seek medical attention, and she died at 2 years of age.
findings.quote: his sister suffered from similar kind of illness but the parents did not seek any medical attention and she died at 2 years of age.

findings.name: Physical examination
findings.result: Height and weight below the fifth percentile, jaundice, abdominal distension, and borderline enlargement of the liver and spleen.
findings.quote: patient was below fifth percentile of height and weight. He is jaundiced and distension of abdomen was also evident. On palpation, liver and spleen appeared to be borderline enlarged.

findings.name: Liver function tests and coagulation studies
findings.result: Alkaline phosphatase 2117 U/L, SGOT 121 U/L, and gamma-GT 301 U/L, with raised total bilirubin and markedly deranged prothrombin time and INR.
findings.quote: Liver function tests demonstrated markedly raised alkaline phosphatase of 2117 U l −1 , SGOT of 121 U l −1 and γ GT of 301 U l −1 . Total bilirubin was also raised. Prothrombin time and INR were also markedly deranged.

findings.name: Serum alpha-fetoprotein
findings.result: Level of 14,831.
findings.quote: serum alpha-feto protein levels were ordered which turned out to be strikingly high with the level of 14,831.

findings.name: Abdominal ultrasound and post-contrast CT
findings.result: Coarse altered liver texture with an irregular nodular appearance and multiple small hypoechoic avascular mass lesions, corresponding to non-enhancing lesions on post-contrast CT without a typical hepatocellular carcinoma enhancement pattern. The portal vein was patent, the spleen was enlarged, and there were no signs of portal hypertension.
findings.quote: coarse altered texture of liver parenchyma with irregular and nodular appearance; multiple small hypoechoic avascular mass lesions were also noted ( Figure 1 ). These correspond to non-enhancing mass lesions in post-contrast CT scan. Typical enhancement pattern of hepatocellular carcinoma was not seen, so these were diagnosed as likely regenerating or dysplastic nodules in the background of cirrhotic liver ( Figure 2a–c . Portal vein was patent and splenomegaly was also noticed. Signs of portal hypertension were not there.

findings.name: Renal ultrasound and post-contrast CT
findings.result: Both kidneys enlarged and echogenic, with poor enhancement and loss of corticomedullary distinction.
findings.quote: Both kidneys were also enlarged and echogenic on ultrasound ( Figure 3 ) These findings ae equivalent to the imaging appearance of kidneys on post-contrast CT scan which show poor enhancement with loss of cortico medullary distinction

findings.name: Chest radiograph, chest CT, and wrist radiographs
findings.result: Expansion of the anterior ends of the ribs, particularly the left lower ribs, with loss of the provisional zone of calcification, widening of the growth plate, and flared, frayed metaphyses.
findings.quote: Chest radiograph anteroposterior view, expansion of the anterior ends of ribs is clearly evident, particularly in the left lower ribs. (b) CT scan chest axial view also shows expansion of anterior ends of ribs consistent with rachitic rosary.(c) X-ray of both wrist joints. There is loss of provisional zone of calcification with widening of growth plate. Metaphysis appears flared and fraying is also evident.

findings.name: Urinary organic acid analysis
findings.result: High level of succinylacetone.
findings.quote: urinary organic acid were then requested which determined high level of succinylacetone.

findings.name: Prior skin lesion course
findings.result: The lesions began as asymptomatic erythematous patches and gradually developed depressed centres.
findings.quote: The lesions initially presented as asymptomatic erythematous patches which had gradually developed depressed centres over time.

findings.name: Prior antituberculous therapy
findings.result: Antituberculous therapy was given for 6 months, and the skin lesions gradually progressed during treatment.
findings.quote: had been given antituberculous therapy for 6 months. However, the skin lesions had gradually progressed during treatment.

findings.name: Facial skin examination
findings.result: Multiple well-defined erythematous plaques on the face; the lesions are depressed with a cliff-drop border.
findings.quote: Multiple, well-defined, erythematous plaques involving the face. (B) The lesions are depressed with a cliff drop border.

findings.name: Neurological examination
findings.result: Sensation was intact, and there was no palpable enlargement of the peripheral nerves.
findings.quote: the patient was found to have intact sensation. There was no palpable enlargement of peripheral nerves.

findings.name: Blood, urine, biochemistry, and antinuclear antibody tests
findings.result: Blood and urine routine examination, biochemistry investigations, and antinuclear antibody test were within normal limits.
findings.quote: Laboratory findings, including blood and urine routine examination, biochemistry investigations and antinuclear antibody test, were within normal limits.

findings.name: Purified protein derivative test
findings.result: Negative.
findings.quote: Purified protein derivative test proved to be negative

findings.name: Chest radiograph
findings.result: Posterior-anterior chest radiograph showed bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.
findings.quote: a posterior-anterior chest X-ray revealed bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy

findings.name: Skin biopsy
findings.result: Numerous compact epithelioid granulomas in the dermis, surrounded by a collar of sparse lymphocytes, with no evidence of acid-fast bacilli, fungi, or polarizable foreign material.
findings.quote: The skin biopsy showed dermal numerous compact epithelioid granulomas, surrounded by a collar of sparse lymphocytes with no evidence of acid-fast bacilli or fungi ( Fig. 1 C and D). There was no polarizable foreign material within the granulomas.

findings.name: Prior symptoms and treatment
findings.result: A 70-year-old man with abdominal pain and headache was prescribed nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and a mucosal protectant for 2 weeks, then referred because the symptoms were unresolved and melena had begun.
findings.quote: A 70‐year‐old man suffering from abdominal pain and headache visited his family doctor and was prescribed non‐steroidal anti‐inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and a mucosal protectant for 2 weeks. He was referred to our hospital because of unresolved symptoms and the onset of melena.

findings.name: Follow-up upper endoscopy and colonoscopy
findings.result: Gastric and duodenal ulcers and esophagitis had healed, but the terminal ileal ulcers and erosions had not improved after nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs were stopped.
findings.quote: we performed a follow‐up EGD and CS, which showed that the gastric and duodenal ulcers and esophagitis had healed (Figure 1d–f ). However, the terminal ileal ulcers and erosions did not improve despite the discontinuation of NSAIDs (Figure 2b,c ).

findings.name: Ileal ulcer biopsy histology
findings.result: Moderate lymphocytic infiltration, with no evidence of malignancy or cytomegalovirus infection.
findings.quote: Hematoxylin Eosin staining of ileal ulcer. It showed moderate infiltration of lymphocytes and no evidence of malignancy or cytomegalovirus infection.

findings.name: Neurologic examination
findings.result: Cognitive decline, mini-mental state examination score 21/25, gait disturbance, and worsening headache.
findings.quote: the patient developed cognitive decline (mini‐mental state examination, 21/25), gait disturbance, and worsening of headache.

findings.name: Head computed tomography
findings.result: High-density areas corresponding to the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli.
findings.quote: Head computed tomography revealed falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli as high‐density areas

findings.name: Serum IgG4
findings.result: 393 mg/dl (normal below 121 mg/dl).
findings.quote: The serum IgG4 level was 393 mg/dl (normal is below 121 mg/dl)

findings.name: Dural biopsy IgG4 immunostaining
findings.result: More than 90 IgG4-positive cells per high-power field, with an IgG4-positive to IgG-positive ratio of 83.2%.
findings.quote: the dural biopsy showed more than 90 IgG4‐positive cells per high power field (Figure 4c ), and the IgG4‐positive:IgG‐positive ratio was 83.2%.

findings.name: Gastrointestinal biopsy IgG4 immunostaining
findings.result: No IgG4-positive cells in the esophagus, stomach, or duodenum. The ileal lesion had more than 20 IgG4-positive cells per high-power field and an IgG4-positive to IgG-positive ratio over 50%.
findings.quote: showed no IgG4‐positive cell infiltration in the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum. However, more than 20 IgG4‐positive cells infiltrated per high power field in the ileal lesion (Figure 2d,e ) where the IgG4‐positive:IgG‐positive ratio was over 50%.

findings.name: Mastectomy specimen histology and axillary lymph nodes

findings.quote: A histological examination revealed poorly differentiated spindle cell tumor proliferation. Fifteen lymph nodes were explored, and involvement was found zero node-negative/15 node explored (0 N-/15 N).

findings.name: Mastectomy specimen immunohistochemistry
findings.result: Focal cytokeratin AE1/AE3, moderate cytoplasmic CK14, nuclear p63, and Ki-67 20%; no CK5/6, CD10, AML, or BCL2 expression; no ER, PR, or HER2 expression

There was a lack of expression of CK5/6, CD10, acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and BCL2. draft.opening: A 34-year-old pregnant woman is found in the first trimester to have a fetal nuchal translucency of 1.8 mm, an absent ductus venosus, and a cystic mass in the thoracic cavity. She continues the pregnancy.
draft.opening_quote: Herein, we present a 34-year-old pregnant woman. The patient initially conceived via artificial insemination. However, her pregnancy was subsequently terminated. Next, she had her second artificial insemination and eventually got pregnant. During the first trimester of pregnancy, a nuchal translucency (NT) measuring 1.8 mm was detected. Moreover, the ductus venous was absent, and a cystic mass was detected in the thoracic cavity. The pregnant woman decided to continue with the pregnancy.
draft.diagnosis_quote: The foetus was diagnosed with SLS due to the coexistence of brachioesophagus, secondary intrathoracic stomach and vertebral anomalies.

encounter.start: First-trimester detection of a fetal thoracic cystic mass
encounter.cutoff: Autopsy after pregnancy termination, when the short oesophagus, intrathoracic stomach, and cervical vertebral anomalies were documented
encounter.cutoff_quote: The foetus was diagnosed with SLS due to the coexistence of brachioesophagus, secondary intrathoracic stomach and vertebral anomalies.

findings.name: First-trimester fetal ultrasound
findings.result: Nuchal translucency 1.8 mm, ductus venosus absent, and a cystic mass in the thoracic cavity
findings.quote: a nuchal translucency (NT) measuring 1.8 mm was detected. Moreover, the ductus venous was absent, and a cystic mass was detected in the thoracic cavity.

findings.name: Fetal ultrasound at 19 weeks' gestation
findings.result: A cystic structure extended from the pharynx to the diaphragm in the right thoracic cavity, with no gastric bubble in the abdominal cavity and no ductus venosus identified
findings.quote: A cystic structure was observed from the pharynx to the diaphragm in the right thoracic cavity. However, there was no gastric bubble in the abdominal cavity. No ductus venous was found.

findings.name: Three-dimensional fetal ultrasound at 23 weeks' gestation
findings.result: The oesophagus measured 1.5 cm and its end was connected to the cystic structure
findings.quote: The oesophagus was short, with a length of 1.5 cm. The end of the oesophagus was connected to the cystic structure

findings.name: Autopsy examination of the stomach
findings.result: The whole stomach lay in the right thoracic cavity and was reversed, with the lesser curvature on the left and the greater curvature on the right
findings.quote: The whole stomach was in the right thoracic cavity with a reversed rotation, thereby suggesting a lesser curvature on the left and a greater curvature on the right.

findings.name: Autopsy examination of the cervical spine
findings.result: Vertebral dysplasia at C2–C6, fusion and disorganization of the C2–C4 vertebral bodies, and a 0.4 × 0.3 cm anterior fissure at C5–C6; spinal cord tissue was normal
findings.quote: Vertebral dysplasia was observed at the C2–C6 levels with C2–C4 vertebral body fusion and disorganization, and there was an anterior fissure at the C5–C6 levels with the defect size was 0.4 × 0.3 cm. However, the spinal cord tissue was normal.

findings.name: Autopsy examination of the oesophagogastric junction
findings.result: The cervical spine defect was closely connected to the serosa at the transition between the oesophagus and cardia, and the cardia was fixed in front of C6
findings.quote: The defect in the cervical spine was closely connected to the serosa of the transitional area of the oesophagus and cardia. The cardia was fixed at the site of cervical spondylolysis in front of the C6 level.

findings.name: Autopsy examination of the diaphragm and upper abdominal organs
findings.result: A dorsal diaphragmatic defect was present; parts of the duodenum and pancreas, the left and caudate lobes of the liver, and the whole spleen lay in the right chest, and the spleen behind the stomach had a poly-spleen malformation
findings.quote: There was a defect in the diaphragm at the dorsal side. Parts of the duodenum, pancreas, left and caudate lobes of the liver and whole spleen were in the right chest. The spleen (with poly-spleen malformation) was behind the stomach.

draft.opening: A 6-year-old boy was seen for lesions in the maxilla and mandible that his parents had noticed 2 months earlier.
draft.opening_quote: A 6-year-old boy had synchronous lesions involving both the maxilla and mandible. His parents noticed the lesions 2 months prior to evaluation.
draft.diagnosis_quote: The combination of histopathologic, radiographic, and clinical features supported a diagnosis of multiple conventional ossifying fibroma.

encounter.start: Initial evaluation, 2 months after the lesions were noticed
encounter.cutoff: GNAS and HRPT2 sequencing of the biopsy tissue
encounter.cutoff_quote: Mutational analysis of GNAS and HRPT2 revealed no genetic abnormality in the lesions.

findings.name: Family history
findings.result: No familial history of jaw disease.
findings.quote: The patient did not have any familial history of jaw disease.

findings.name: Physical examination
findings.result: Firm, non-fluctuant lesions with bilateral mandibular buccal expansion from the deciduous canine to the deciduous molar; overlying mucosa intact.
findings.quote: On examination, the lesions were firm and non-fluctuant, and bilateral mandibular buccal bone expansion was found extending from the deciduous canine to the deciduous molar. The overlying mucosa was intact.

findings.name: Panoramic radiography
findings.result: A large lesion extended from the right ascending mandibular ramus to the left, with central heterogeneous mineralization and a thin marginal radiolucent rim with a well-demarcated sclerotic border.
findings.quote: Panoramic radiography revealed a large lesion extending from the right ascending mandibular ramus to the left ascending mandibular ramus. The lesion consisted of a central heterogeneous mineralization and a thin marginal radiolucent area with a well-demarcated sclerotic border.

findings.name: Radiographic dental findings
findings.result: Several tooth germs were displaced, roots of multiple primary teeth were resorbed, and permanent molars were displaced, including the second molar into the ascending ramus.
findings.quote: Several tooth germs were displaced, and roots of multiple primary teeth were resorbed. The permanent molar teeth were significantly displaced, particularly the second molar, which was displaced into the ascending ramus

findings.name: Computed tomography
findings.result: Thinned cortex along the inferior mandibular border with alveolar expansion beside a mixed radiopaque mass; a displaced tooth germ extended into the maxillary sinus.
findings.quote: A CT scan confirmed thinned bony cortex of the inferior mandibular border and alveolar bone expansion near the mixed radiopaque mass (Figure 2 B). A displaced tooth germ grew into the maxillary sinus

findings.name: Serum biochemistry
findings.result: Serum calcium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase, and PTH were within normal limits.
findings.quote: Blood tests (serum calcium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase, and PTH) were within normal limits.

findings.name: Incisional biopsy
findings.result: Mandibular and maxillary specimens showed a similar pattern of fibrous tissue rich in fibroblasts with spherical calcifications.
findings.quote: Incisional biopsies were performed in the mandibular and the maxillary lesions, and both specimens showed a similar histopathologic pattern. The lesions were mainly composed of fibrous tissue rich in fibroblasts with spherical calcifications.

findings.name: GNAS and HRPT2 sequencing
findings.result: No genetic abnormality in the lesions.
findings.quote: Mutational analysis of GNAS and HRPT2 revealed no genetic abnormality in the lesions.

encounter.start: Referral with constant right proximal thigh pain progressing for 8 years
encounter.cutoff: End of the initial imaging, laboratory, genetic, and biopsy assessment
encounter.cutoff_quote: With special emphasis on the uneven surface of the affected bone on X-ray (Fig. 3 ), the diagnosis of melorheostosis, which was fully compatible with the relatively unremarkable histology, was found to be the most plausible diagnosis.

findings.name: Pain pattern
findings.result: Pain aggravated at night and moderately relieved by physical activity and cold baths.
findings.quote: The limb pain was aggravated at night and was moderately relieved during physical activity and by cold baths.

findings.name: Right thigh examination
findings.result: No skin lesions, café au lait spots, redness, increased temperature, or swelling in the right thigh; leg length unequal but within normality.
findings.quote: A clinical examination revealed no skin lesions, café au lait spots, or redness; there was no increased temperature or swelling in her right thigh. Leg length was unequal but within normality.

findings.name: MRI and PET-CT of the femur
findings.result: Significantly increased cortical thickness of the right femoral diaphysis partially obliterating the medullary cavity, with an uneven sclerotic surface.
findings.quote: Magnetic resonance (MR) and positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) scans revealed significant increased cortical thickness in the right femoral diaphysis that partially obliterated the medullary cavity (Fig. 1 ). The surface of the sclerotic bone was uneven.

findings.name: Radiograph of the right femoral shaft
findings.result: Irregular hyperostosis of the right femoral shaft.
findings.quote: X-ray of the patient’s right femoral shaft showing irregular hyperostosis

findings.name: Bone scintigraphy
findings.result: Increased tracer uptake in most of the right femoral shaft.
findings.quote: A Tc 99 -bone scan showed a pathological increase in uptake in most of the right femoral shaft (Fig. 2 ).

findings.name: Biochemical bone markers
findings.result: Biochemical bone markers were normal, including alkaline phosphatase.
findings.quote: Biochemical bone markers were normal, including normal alkaline phosphatase.

findings.name: GNAS1 and SQSTM1 mutation screening
findings.result: GNAS1 activating mutation R201 was negative in peripheral blood, and SQSTM1 mutation screening was negative.
findings.quote: Screening for the GNAS1 activating mutation R201 was negative in peripheral blood; as was mutation screening of the SQSTM1 gene

findings.name: Bone biopsy
findings.result: Thickened bone springs with preserved lamellar structure and slightly accentuated cement lines; no fibrosis, inflammation, increased alcian positivity, or signs of malignancy or neoplasia.
findings.quote: A bone biopsy was performed and showed thickened bone springs with preserved lamellar structure and slightly accentuated cement lines. findings.name: Emergency presentation
findings.result: Acute chest tightness, burning pain radiating from the chest to both upper extremities, sensory impairment at the nipple level (T4), and bilateral arm paresis within several minutes.
findings.quote: was admitted to the emergency department (ED) at the University Clinical Centre (UCC) in Gdańsk with the following acute symptoms: tightness in the chest, burning pain radiating from the chest to both upper extremities, and sensory impairment at the nipple level (T4). After several minutes, bilateral arm paresis appeared.

findings.name: Limb strength
findings.result: Lower left extremity strength fell from 5 to 2 on Lovett’s scale within hours, then during the stay the lower right fell from 5 to 3, the lower left from 2 to 0, and both upper extremities from 5 to 3.
findings.quote: A few hours later, the strength of his lower left extremity deteriorated (from 5 to 2 on Lovett’s scale) [ 6 , 7 ]. During the patient’s hospital stay, a constant weakening of the lower extremities (the right going from 5 to 3 on Lovett’s scale, the left going from 2 to 0 on Lovett’s scale) [ 6 , 7 ] followed by a weakening of the upper extremities (both going from 5 to 3 on Lovett’s scale) [ 6 , 7 ] was observed.

findings.name: Cervical spinal cord MRI
findings.result: Inflammatory focus in the central part of the C5/C6 spinal cord; contrast agents did not reveal activity features.
findings.quote: On MR images, a radiologist found an inflammatory focus in the central part of the C5/C6 spinal cord ( Figure 1 ). The use of contrast agents did not reveal any activity features.

findings.name: Brain and thoracic spine MRI
findings.result: No lesions on later MR images of the cerebrum and thoracic spine.
findings.quote: The MR images of the cerebrum and the thoracic spine acquired later showed no lesions.

findings.name: Cerebrospinal fluid protein and albumin
findings.result: Total protein 0.91 g/L and albumin 656.7 mg/L, both reported as elevated.
findings.quote: The biochemical CSF examination revealed elevated total protein (0.91 g/L) and elevated albumin (656.7 mg/L) levels.

findings.name: Cerebrospinal fluid oligoclonal bands and microbiology
findings.result: Intradural type 4 oligoclonal band synthesis was not observed. CSF culture and PCR for pathogens were negative, and the fluid culture was negative.
findings.quote: Intradural type 4 oligoclonal band synthesis, as defined in the Charcot Foundation standards, was not observed. The CSF culture test and PCR test for the presence of pathogens in CSF were negative. The fluid culture test was negative.

findings.name: Aquaporin-4 antibody
findings.result: Negative.
findings.quote: The aquaporin-4 antibody test was negative.

findings.name: MOG antibody
findings.result: 1:10 on 13 October 2022, described as slightly elevated; repeat on 18 October 2022 was <1:10, described as unfavorable.
findings.quote: The result of the anti-MOG antibody test performed on 13 October 2022 was slightly elevated (1:10). The result of another trial, conducted on 18 October 2022, was <1:10, which is described as unfavorable.

encounter.start: Hospital presentation with worsening temporal disorientation and unsteady gait
encounter.cutoff: Immunohistochemical staining of the brain biopsy
encounter.cutoff_quote: Immunohistochemical staining with antibodies against TG confirmed the diagnosis of cerebral toxoplasmosis, highlighting the free tachyzoites

findings.name: Rheumatoid arthritis medication history
findings.result: Rheumatoid arthritis diagnosed 10 years earlier, treated with prednisolone 10 mg daily, leflunomide 20 mg daily, and methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly; adalimumab 40 mg/0.4 mL every two weeks was added 2 months earlier and the other drugs were continued
findings.quote: The patient had been diagnosed with RA 10 years earlier and was on chronic treatment with oral prednisolone (10 mg daily), leflunomide (20 mg daily) and methotrexate (7.5 mg once every week). Due to progressive joint pain and deformity, adalimumab (40 mg/0.4 mL once every two weeks) was added to her regimen 2 months earlier, while continuing to receive methotrexate, leflunomide and prednisolone.

findings.name: Neurologic examination
findings.result: Moderate left hemiparesis, grade 3, with no spatial disorientation, sensory disturbances, or cranial nerve injuries
findings.quote: Neurologic examination revealed moderate left hemiparesis (grade 3 in the medical research council [MRS] scale), with no evidence of spatial disorientation, sensory disturbances or cranial nerve injuries.

findings.name: Complete blood count
findings.result: White blood cell count 9100 µL, neutrophils 8120 µL (89%), lymphocytes 600 µL (7%)
findings.quote: a normal white blood cell count (9100 µL) with relative neutrophilia (8120 µL, 89%) and relative lymphopenia (600 µL, 7%)

findings.name: Body temperature
findings.result: Afebrile, 36.4 °C
findings.quote: the patient was afebrile (T = 36.4 °C)

findings.name: HIV and Toxoplasma serology
findings.result: HIV type 1 seronegative; detectable serum IgG antibodies to Toxoplasma gondii and negative IgM
findings.quote: The patient was seronegative for HIV type 1 and had detectable serum Immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies to TG, although Immunoglobulin M (IgM) titers were negative.

findings.name: Brain CT
findings.result: Focal space-occupying hypodense lesion in the right basal ganglia with surrounding edema, effacement of the ipsilateral sulci, ventricular buckling without hydrocephalus, and mild midline shift to the left
findings.quote: Computed tomography (CT) scan of the brain revealed the presence of a focal space-occupying hypodense lesion in the right basal ganglia, surrounded by edema. The lesion caused mass effect with effacement of ipsilateral cerebral sulci, buckling of the ventricular system (without hydrocephalus) and mild deviation of midline structures to the left

findings.name: Brain MRI
findings.result: Lesion relatively heterogeneous on T2/FLAIR with marginal enhancement after gadolinium; perfusion-weighted imaging showed a significant decrease of cerebral blood flow (CBV) within the lesion
findings.quote: On magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), the lesion was relatively heterogeneous on T2/FLAIR and exhibited marginal enhancement following gadolinium injection. Perfusion-weighted imaging demonstrated significant decrease of cerebral blood flow (CBV) within the lesion

findings.name: Brain biopsy
findings.result: Cysts containing bradyzoites and free tachyzoites throughout the sample
findings.quote: A brain biopsy was later performed and revealed not only cysts containing bradyzoites but also free microorganisms (tachyzoites) across the sample.

draft.opening: A 38-year-old woman was referred from the general outpatient clinic with a one-month history of recurrent difficulty breathing, chest pain, headaches, blurring of vision, and dizziness, and a blood pressure of 260/150 mmHg.
draft.opening_quote: This patient is a 38-year-old housewife who was referred from the general out-patient clinic on account of a one-month history of recurrent difficulty in breathing, associated with chest pain, recurrent headaches, blurring of vision, and dizziness with blood pressure of 260/150 mmHg.
draft.diagnosis_quote: A possible diagnosis of left intrathoracic ectopic kidney with chronic kidney disease secondary to possible renovascular hypertension was made.

encounter.start: Referral from the general out-patient clinic
encounter.cutoff: Imaging diagnosis at the end of the admission workup, before maintenance haemodialysis
encounter.cutoff_quote: A possible diagnosis of left intrathoracic ectopic kidney with chronic kidney disease secondary to possible renovascular hypertension was made.

findings.name: Past medical history
findings.result: Diagnosed as hypertensive five years before presentation and not compliant with antihypertensive medications. No known family history of hypertension.
findings.quote: She was diagnosed as hypertensive five years before presentation but had not been compliant with antihypertensive medications. There was no known family history of hypertension.

findings.name: Presenting symptoms
findings.result: One-month history of recurrent difficulty in breathing, chest pain, recurrent headaches, blurring of vision, and dizziness, with blood pressure 260/150 mmHg.
findings.quote: a one-month history of recurrent difficulty in breathing, associated with chest pain, recurrent headaches, blurring of vision, and dizziness with blood pressure of 260/150 mmHg

findings.name: Associated symptoms
findings.result: Orthopnoea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, no cough, mild central chest pain, and progressively worsening bilateral leg swelling with reduced urine volume.
findings.quote: There was a history of orthopnoea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea. She had no associated cough but had a mild centrally located chest pain. There was a history of bilateral leg swelling which has been progressively worsening and associated with diminution in urine volume.

findings.name: Cardiorespiratory examination
findings.result: Respiratory rate 50 cycles/minute, reduced breath sounds in the left lower lung zones, and bibasal fine crepitations. Pulse 118 beats/minute, normal volume and regular, with clinical evidence of arterial wall thickening. Blood pressure 220/120 mmHg, a fourth heart sound, and a loud aortic component of the second heart sound.
findings.quote: Her respiratory rate was 50 cycles/minute with reduced breath sounds in the left lower lung zones and bibasal fine crepitations. The pulse rate was 118 beats/minute, normal volume and regular. There was clinical evidence of arterial wall thickening. Blood pressure was 220/120 mmHg with a fourth heart sound and loud aortic component of the second heart sound.

findings.name: Serum chemistry
findings.result: Predialysis creatinine 900 μmol/L (reference 53–115), urea 30 mmol/L (reference 2.1–7.1), sodium 136 mmol/L, potassium 4.0 mmol/L, chloride 98 mmol/L, and bicarbonate 28 mmol/L.
findings.quote: E/U/C (predialysis). Creatinine: 900 μ mol/L (53–115). Urea: 30 mmol/L (2.1–7.1). Na: 136 mmol/L (135–145). K: 4.0 mmol/L (3.2–5.0). Cl: 98 mmol/L (96–108). HCO 3 : 28 mmol/L (22–28).

findings.name: Urinalysis
findings.result: Proteinuria (++) and no haematuria.
findings.quote: Urinalysis showed ++ proteinuria, no haematuria.

findings.name: Renal ultrasound and renal artery Doppler
findings.result: Right kidney 8.63 × 4.59 × 5.07 cm with loss of corticomedullary differentiation; right renal artery velocity 73.9 cm/second and resistive index 0.9. The upper margin of the left kidney appeared intrathoracic and could not be well deciphered; the left kidney was hypoechoic with complete loss of corticomedullary differentiation, and left renal artery Doppler velocity was 195 cm/min.
findings.quote: renal USS/Doppler-right kidney measured 8.63 × 4.59 × 5.07 cm. There was loss of corticomedullary differentiation. Doppler insonation of the renal artery showed a velocity of 73.9 cm/second and a resistive index of 0.9 suggesting renal intraparenchymal disease. The upper margin of the left kidney appeared to be intrathoracic and could not be well deciphered. The echotexture was hypoechoic with complete loss of corticomedullary differentiation. Doppler insonation of the left renal artery showed a velocity of 195 cm/min consistent with a stenotic artery.

findings.name: Abdominal CT
findings.result: Scanogram showed a left intrathoracic well-marginated upper-border mass obscuring the left hemidiaphragm medially and the cardiac apex. Contiguous slices showed the left kidney in an abnormal location in the left hemithorax, between the cardiac silhouette and the spleen. The right kidney was normally located with major blood vessels appearing normal, and the left kidney was slightly bigger than the right.
findings.quote: the scanogram showed a left intrathoracic well-marginated upper border mass obscuring the left hemidiaphragm medially and obscuring the cardiac apex. Contiguous slices showed the left kidney to be in an abnormal location in the left hemithorax sitting between the cardiac silhouette and spleen. The right kidney was in its normal location with major blood vessels appearing normal. The left kidney was slightly bigger than the right one

findings.name: Excisional biopsy of a left inguinal lymph node
findings.result: The node was extensively involved by small compact nonnecrotizing granulomas. GMS stain showed no fungal organisms and AFB stain showed no acid-fast organisms. No morphologic or immunophenotypic evidence of malignancy.

findings.name: Symptom timeline
findings.result: Symptoms began three weeks before the emergency visit and worsened with intense physical activity.
findings.quote: Symptoms began three weeks before ED presentation, worsening with intense physical activity.

findings.name: Cardiac and abdominal examination
findings.result: Regular heart rate and rhythm with a few extrasystolic beats, normal S1 and S2, grade 3/6 systolic murmur loudest at the pulmonary focus, no gallops or rubs, symmetrical peripheral pulses, and mild hepatomegaly.
findings.quote: regular heart rate and rhythm, interrupted by few extra systolic beats, with normal S1 and S2 and cardiac systolic murmur graded 3/6 Levine (highest at pulmonary focus) without gallops and rubs. The peripheral pulses were present and symmetrical. There was mild hepatomegaly.

findings.name: Blood tests
findings.result: Hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL, GPT-transaminase 43 U/L, and NT-proBNP 4019 pg/mL. Coagulation parameters, renal function tests, C-reactive protein, and high-sensitivity troponin were normal.
findings.quote: The blood exams showed mild anemia (hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL) and augmentation of GPT-transaminases (43 U/L). Coagulation parameters, renal function tests, C-Reactive Protein and high-sensitivity troponin were normal, but NT-proBNP was elevated (4019 pg/mL).

findings.name: Electrocardiogram
findings.result: Sinus rhythm with normal PR and QTc intervals, right bundle block with ventricular repolarization abnormalities in the right leads, and isolated monomorphic premature ventricular contractions, often in bigeminy.
findings.quote: ECG revealed sinus rhythm with normal PR and QTc intervals, right bundle block with ventricular repolarization abnormalities in the right leads and isolated monomorphic premature ventricular contractions (PVCs), often organized in bigeminy rhythm

findings.name: Echocardiogram
findings.result: Rounded, lobulated 3.5 × 4 cm mass with clear margins and inhomogeneous content, adherent to the infundibular septum by a pedicle. Right ventricular outflow maximum instantaneous systolic gradient 80 mmHg, with the pulmonary valve spared. Right atrial area 23.5 cm²; right ventricular telediastolic area 23 cm² and telesystolic area 19 cm²; fractional area change 18.6%.
findings.quote: Echocardiogram identified a rounded and lobulated voluminous (3.5 × 4 cm) mass with clear margins and inhomogeneous content, adherent to the infundibular septum through a pedicle. The right ventricle outflow tract (RVOT) showed a severe obstruction with a maximum instantaneous systolic gradient of 80 mmHg, sparing the pulmonary valve ( Figure 2 and Figure 3 ). The right atrium (Area 23.5 cm 2 ) and ventricle (tele-diastolic area was 23 cm 2 and tele-systolic 19 cm 2 ) were dilated with a severe systolic dysfunction (Fractional Area Change of 18.6%).

findings.name: Contrast CT
findings.result: Heterogeneously enhancing soft-tissue mass occupying the right ventricular outflow tract, with no evidence of pulmonary embolization.
findings.quote: Contrast CT scan confirmed the presence of a heterogeneously enhancing soft-tissue mass occupying the RVOT with no evidence of pulmonary embolization

findings.name: Intraoperative inspection
findings.result: A 4 cm × 4 cm gelatinous mass with a pedicle arising in the right outflow a few millimeters from the pulmonary valve and projecting toward the valve, obstructing the right ventricular outflow.
findings.quote: The mass (4 cm × 4 cm) had a pedicle originating in the right outflow a few mm from the pulmonary valve and jutting towards the pulmonary valve itself, obstructing the right ventricle outflow. The rather gelatinous mass was removed with the pedicle

findings.name: Pathology of the excised mass
findings.result: Whitish ovoid nodule, 3 cm in diameter, with a smooth surface. Histology showed a myxoid background with mostly loose, multifocally denser proliferation of single cells or cords, a low mitotic index, and no atypia.
findings.quote: The surgical mass was a whitish ovoid nodule, 3 cm in diameter, with a smooth surface ( Figure 5 A). Histological examination shows in a myxoid background cell proliferation, mostly loose, multifocally more densified, of single cells or in cords with a low mitotic index, in the absence of atypia

draft.opening_quote: We report the case of a 6-year-old Caucasian girl hospitalized for right orbital preseptal cellulitis, requiring intravenous antibiotic therapy. Medical history included adenotonsillectomy at the age of 2 years and a second adenoid resection at the age of 5 years. She had no ophthalmological history. Upon emergency room admission, she presented erythematous, sensitive, and edematous eyelids that had developed after 5 days of fever (up to 39.5 °C) and 2 weeks of unilateral clear right eye tearing.

findings.name: Bacterial cultures and MRSA screening
findings.result: Blood cultures, eye-discharge swabs, and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus screening were negative.
findings.quote: Blood cultures and bacteriological swabs of the eye discharge as well as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) screening were all negative.

findings.name: Epstein–Barr virus serology
findings.result: Positive, with highly elevated immunoglobulin G and immunoglobulin M antibodies.
findings.quote: EBV serology came back positive with highly elevated antibodies (immunoglobulines G and M), compatible with an acute infection.
